en: It's quite remarkable how different genres of music can spark unique feelings, emotions, and memories. Studies have shown that music can reduce stress and anxiety before surgeries and we are all attracted toward our own unique life soundtrack.
zh: 这个opening paragraph为整篇文章的central thesis做了essential groundwork。通过establish音乐的universal emotional impact，作者create了receptive mindset for readers。Scientific reference to stress reduction directly foreshadows文章主旨中的stress reduction这个key benefit。这个paragraph的strategic value在于它avoid了abrupt dive into classical music，instead选择from broad musical landscape gradually zoom in，making the eventual focus on Mozart feel like natural progression而非arbitrary choice。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: If you're looking to alleviate stress, you might want to give classical music a try.
zh: 这个short paragraph在文章structure中扮演critical transitional role。它完成了from generic music benefits到classical music specific effects的pivot。对于overall thesis，这个paragraph establish了focus—所有subsequent discussion of stress reduction, cognitive function, blood pressure, and sleep都是在elaborate这个initial recommendation。它的brevity本身是deliberate choice，因为author想要create momentum toward详细的scientific explanations，而不是在这里bog down with details。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The sounds of classical music produce a calming effect letting loose pleasure-inducing dopamine(多巴胺) in the brain that helps control attention, learning and emotional responses. It can also turn down the body's stress response, resulting in an overall happier mood. It turns out a pleasant mood can lead to clarity in a person's thinking.
zh: 这个paragraph提供了first substantive scientific explanation for文章主旨中提到的stress reduction和cognitive function improvement。通过introduce dopamine as biological agent，作者ground abstract benefits in concrete neuroscience。这个paragraph也establish了template for后续paragraphs—present scientific mechanism, connect to observable benefit。它的position after the brief recommendation创造了classic expository pattern: claim, then evidence。这个详细的mechanistic account lends credibility到整个argument about classical music's health benefits。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Although there are many great composers of classical music like Bach, Beethoven and Handel, none of these artists' music seems to have the same health effects as Mozart's does. According to researchers, listening to Mozart can increase brain wave activity and improve cognitive function. Another study found that the distinctive features of Mozart's music trigger parts of the brain that are responsible for high-level mental functions. Even maternity wards use Mozart to help newborn babies adapt to life outside of the mother's belly.
zh: 这个paragraph是文章的turning point，因为它从general classical music narrow down到Mozart specifically，directly addressing文章主旨中particularly Mozart's compositions这个key specification。通过cite multiple research studies和concrete application in maternity wards，作者build compelling case for Mozart's unique status。这个paragraph也expand cognitive function这个concept from前段的general clarity到specific high-level mental functions。它的strategic position in middle of article让它serve as centerpiece—前面establish了why classical music matters，这里explain为什么Mozart特别重要，后续paragraphs会continue exploring other health dimensions。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: It has been found that listening to classical music significantly reduces a person's blood pressure. Researchers believe that the calming sounds of classical music may help your heart recover from stress. Classical music can also be a great tool to help people who have trouble sleeping. One study found that students who had trouble sleeping slept better while they were listening to classical music.
zh: 这个paragraph继续expand文章主旨中significant health benefits的catalog，adding lower blood pressure和better sleep quality到已讨论的stress reduction和cognitive improvements。它的strategic placement after Mozart-specific paragraph是deliberate—revert回broader classical music而非only Mozart，suggesting这些cardiovascular和sleep benefits可能apply to classical music generally。这个paragraph也strengthen overall argument through cite multiple studies，maintaining consistent evidential rigor。它successfully bridge cognitive/emotional benefits和physical health outcomes，demonstrating classical music的holistic impact on human wellbeing。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Whether classical music is something that you listen to on a regular basis or not, it wouldn't hurt to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find soothing. You will be surprised at how good it makes you feel and the potentially positive change in your health.
zh: 这个closing paragraph完成了文章的rhetorical arc from observation到evidence再到action。它deliberately step back from Mozart-specific和classical-specific claims，returning to broader soothing music这个category，making recommendation maximally accessible。对文章主旨而言，这个paragraph不add new specific benefits，但它serve crucial function of translating accumulated evidence into practical life advice。Through combining inclusive tone, low-commitment suggestion, and promise of multiple benefits，it provide satisfying closure while motivating readers toward behavior change。这个paragraph也subtly validate整个preceding argument—如果benefits weren't significant，wouldn't be worth this concluding emphasis。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In the city of Athens, Georgia, there exists a rather curious local landmark—a large white oak that is almost universally stated to own itself. Because of this, it is considered one of the most famous trees in the world. So how did this tree come to own itself and the land around it?
zh: 本段为全文建立了 legend 的叙述对象，而后文将从温情起源逐步转向 historical doubt，形成由相信到质疑的主线。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Sometime in the 19th century a Georgian called Colonel William Jackson reportedly took a liking to the said tree and endeavored to protect it from any danger. As to why he loved it so, the earliest documented account of this story is an anonymously written front page article in the Athens Weekly Banner published on August 12, 1890. It states, "Col. Jackson had watched the tree grow from his childhood, and grew to love it almost as he would a human. Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains, and out of its highest branches he had many a time gotten the eggs of the feathered singers. He watched its growth, and when reaching a ripe old age he saw the tree standing in its magnificent proportions, he was pained to think that after his death it would fall into the hands of those who might destroy it."
zh: 本段先构建一个动人的 origin story，使读者理解为何 Jackson 似乎会保护树；但其 anonymous source 也为后文的证伪埋下伏笔。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Towards this end, Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree and a little land around it to the tree itself. The deed read, "W. H. Jackson for and in consideration of the great affection which he bears the said tree, and his great desire to see it protected has conveyed unto the said oak tree entire possession of itself and of all land within eight feet of it on all sides."
zh: 本段给出了“树拥有自己”这一传说的直接解释，是前半部分 legend 的核心情节，也成为后文法律与史实调查的对象。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In time, the tree came to be something of a tourist attraction, known as The Tree That Owns Itself. However, in the early 20th century, the tree started showing signs of its slow death, with little that could be done about it. Father time comes for us all eventually, even our often long lived, tall and leafy fellow custodians(看管者) of Earth. Finally, on October 9, 1942, the over 30 meter tall and 200-400 year old tree fell, rumor has it, as a result of a severe windstorm and/or via having previously died and its roots rotted.
zh: 本段结束原树的生命历程，并制造传承问题：既然原树已倒下，那个关于土地和身份的传奇将如何延续。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: About four years later, members of the Junior Ladies Garden Club (who'd tended to the tree before its unfortunate death) tracked down a small tree grown from a nut taken from the original tree. And so it was that on October 9, 1946, under the direction of Professor Roy Bowden of the College of Agriculture at the University of Georgia, this little tree was transplanted to the location of its ancestor. A couple of months later, an official ceremony was held featuring none other than the Mayor of Athens, Robert L McWhorter, to commemorate the occasion.
zh: 本段让故事从死亡转向 renewal，解释了今天人们仍能看到这棵树的原因，并为“儿子是否继承土地”铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: This new tree became known as The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself and it was assumed that, as the original tree's heir, it naturally inherited the land it stood on. Of course, there are many dozens of other trees known to exist descending from the original, as people taking a nut from it to grow elsewhere was a certainty. That said, to date, none of the original tree's other children have petitioned the courts for their share of the land, so it seems all good. In any event, The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself still stands today, though often referred to simply as The Tree That Owns Itself.
zh: 本段完成了传说在现实中的延续，同时以 other children 和 courts 的幽默表述，暗示所谓继承权其实缺乏严肃的法律基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: This all brings us around to whether Jackson ever actually gave legal ownership of the tree to itself in the first place and whether such a deed is legally binding.
zh: 本段是全文结构的分水岭：前六段讲故事的形成与延续，后文则以 evidence 检验故事，从而服务文章“传说或为虚构”的主旨。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Well, to begin with, it turns out Jackson only spent about three years of his life in Athens, starting at the age of 43 from 1829 to 1832, sort of dismissing the idea that he loved the tree from spending time under it as a child and watching it grow, and then worrying about what would happen to it after he died. Further, an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on.
zh: 本段首次给出有力的 factual contradiction，使温情传说开始崩塌，也为最终“记者杜撰”的判断提供证据链。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: He did live on a lot of land directly next to it for those three years, but whether he owned that land or not isn't clear. Whatever the case, in 1832 a four acre parcel, which included the land the tree was on and the neighboring land Jackson lived on, among others, was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward. In the transaction, Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200 (about $31, 000 today), either for the property itself or simply in compensation for improvements Jackson had made on the lot. In the end, whether he ever owned the neighboring lot or was simply allowed to use it while he allegedly worked at the University, he definitely never owned the lot the tree grew on, which is the most important bit for the topic at hand.
zh: 本段进一步削弱 deed 的可能性：一个不拥有该地的人，无从把树和土地 legally convey 给树本身。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: After Professor Ward purchased the land, Jackson and his family purchased a 655 acre parcel a few miles away and moved there. Ten years later, in 1844, Jackson seemed to have come into financial difficulties and had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage. Thus, had he owned some land in Athens itself, including the land the tree sat on, presumably he would have sold it to raise funds or otherwise had it taken as well.
zh: 本段从土地档案扩展到经济经历，以旁证强化前文结论，使 Jackson 曾拥有树地的说法更加难以成立。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: And whatever the case there, Jackson would have known property taxes needed to be paid on the deeded land for the tree to be truly secure in its future. Yet no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this.
zh: 本段补充法律实践层面的漏洞，说明该故事不仅史料不足，而且缺乏维持土地所有权所必需的机制。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: On top of all this, there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed, despite the fact that deed records in Athens go back many decades before Jackson's death in 1876 and that it was supposed to have existed in 1890 in the archives according to the original anonymous news reporter who claims to have seen it.
zh: 本段提供了最直接的否定性证据，几乎从根本上动摇了传说的法律基础，并推动文章接近最终结论。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: As you might imagine from all of this, few give credit to this side of the story. So how did all of this come about then?
zh: 本段承上启下：它收束对 deed 的质疑，并自然引出作者关于 anonymous journalist 可能杜撰故事的解释。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author at the Athens Weekly Banner in the aforementioned 1890 front page article titled "Deeded to Itself", which by the way contained several elements that are much more easily proved to be false. As to why the author would do this, it's speculated perhaps it was a 19th century version of a click-bait thought exercise on whether it would be legal for someone to deed such a non-conscious living thing to itself or not.
zh: 本段揭示全文最核心的真相：温情的 self-owning tree story 很可能并非历史事实，而是新闻作者制造出来的 imaginative fiction。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Whatever the case, the next known instance of the Tree That Owns Itself being mentioned wasn't until 1901 in the Centennial Edition of that same paper, the Athens Weekly Banner. This featured another account very clearly just copying the original article published about a decade before, only slightly reworded. The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner, again very clearly copying the original account, only slightly reworded, the 19th century equivalent of re-posts when the audience has forgotten about the original.
zh: 本段补全传说扩散机制，并最终呼应文章主旨：一个可能由记者虚构的故事，经由 repeated reporting 变成了广为人知的 local legend。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The term "environmentalist" can mean different things. It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems. In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change.
zh: 本段为全文建立了 environmentalism 的双重内涵：传统生态保护与现代气候治理。正因为两种关注点并不完全相同，后文才会出现围绕 nuclear energy 的立场分裂，所以它是文章论证的 conceptual foundation。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.
zh: 本段将第一段的词义演变转化为 nuclear debate，正式提出文章需要解决的问题。它使全文从“什么是 environmentalist”进入“在气候目标下是否应使用核能”的 argument framework。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn't worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy. The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.
zh: 本段完整展开第二段所说的 split，并首次呈现作者后文将重点论证的现实问题：renewables 的 intermittency。第二派提出的 backup power 逻辑，为文章最终支持“核能与可再生能源并用”埋下了论证主线。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn't an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it's a valuable option to have if we're serious about reaching carbon neutrality.
zh: 本段通过权威人士的观点增强第二派论证的 credibility，并把讨论目标明确指向 carbon neutrality。它显示文章并非简单鼓吹核能，而是将其定位为严肃气候战略中的 practical option。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: "Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables," he said. "If you don't believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear."
zh: 本段把“是否需要核能”的价值争论，收束为“100% renewables 是否可实现”的可验证问题。它是全文的 argumentative hinge，因为第六至第九段将用现实案例检验这一可行性，并间接加强核能必要性的论点。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years. But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal. Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities.
zh: 本段为作者的中心立场提供第一层现实证据：局部的 renewable success 不等于大范围的 universal feasibility。它削弱了“只靠可再生能源即可”的绝对论断，并为德国这一更具代表性的大国案例做好铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy. Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables. Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010, and renewables provided 46% of the country's electricity in 2019.
zh: 本段选取德国这一高代表性案例，并先确认其 renewable expansion 的成绩，从而避免文章显得片面否定绿色能源。更重要的是，它建立了后文反转所需的基线：即使在积极转型且成果显著的国家，100% renewable path 仍可能面临深层困难。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But progress has halted in recent years. The instability of renewables doesn't just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity. Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas. The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests.
zh: 本段是全文支撑中心论点的核心 evidence：它具体说明即使 renewables 增长迅速，也难以单独稳定满足大型工业社会的能源需求。尤其 factories still run on coal and gas 的结果表明，缺少可靠补充电源和配套系统时，绿色转型未必能顺利降低化石燃料依赖。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The result is that Germany's greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010—slower than the EU average of 13.5%.
zh: 本段以量化结果收束德国案例，验证前文关于 renewable-only transition 困难的论述。它并未直接断言 nuclear 必不可少，但通过德国减排落后于 EU average 的事实，强化了文章主旨：要可靠实现 carbon neutrality，仅依赖 renewables 可能不足，nuclear energy 值得作为补充方案考虑。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The Sun Is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny.
zh: 这一段承担 introduction 功能，它先亮明作者对作品的肯定态度。它为后文的 character analysis、阅读体验以及对 romance value 的反思提供了总领性的评价框架。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living illegally in America, not by choice exactly. Her parents brought her over and created the situation she strives to be out of.
zh: 本段为 romance story 注入严肃的现实背景，说明 Natasha 并非只在经历甜蜜爱情。她的 immigration struggle 也为第四段的 deportation crisis 埋下伏笔，使读者理解这场相遇为何如此紧迫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Daniel is an American born of Korean immigrants. He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha dismisses through scientific reasoning.
zh: 本段建立了小说最重要的人物张力：romantic optimism 对阵 rational skepticism。这种冲突不仅推动情节，也呼应评论者后来从轻视 romance 到认可其价值的观念转变。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Daniel and Natasha meet by coincidence on the streets of New York on the day that she is to be deported. She doesn't tell him that but does allow him to keep her company while he tries to get her to fall in love with him over the course of the day.
zh: 本段从人物设定转入核心 plot，具体说明两位主人公如何相遇以及爱情为何必须迅速发生。它把 fate 与现实危机结合起来，为评论者后文投入这段 romance 提供了叙事基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Natasha is me. I found her so similar to myself. She's scientifically-minded, practical, somewhat cynical, and always skeptical. Her obsession with the universe through a scientific lens is infectious and I adore Daniel seeing that too.
zh: 本段解释了评论者为何能被这部 romance novel 打动：她原本就站在 Natasha 的 rational position 上。正因她与 skeptical heroine 如此相似，后文她接受爱情“魔力”的转变才更有说服力。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Daniel is charming and passionate and has a way with words that even cracks Natasha's tough outer shell. By the end of the book I fell in love with both of them.
zh: 这一段补足了 Daniel 的人物价值，并说明这段爱情为何可信、为何动人。Daniel 对 Natasha 的影响，使前文的 fate-versus-science conflict 开始向情感融合发展，同时强化书评的赞美立场。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: I used to find romance stories to always be cheap or laughable. I think now I can see the value in escaping into a story of pure optimism. I got lost in The Sun Is Also a Star and finished it cover to cover in a weekend. I couldn't wait to get to what I hoped would be a happy ending.
zh: 本段是全文的核心论证段，它最完整地回应文章主旨：小说改变了评论者对 romance literature 的看法。前面的人物认同与情节吸引力，在此被提升为对浪漫文学价值的明确判断。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: It's nice every once in a while to give in to magic. It doesn't have to be a hard fantasy novel with actual spells, it can be the magic found between two people who just have that special something. That chemistry that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other.
zh: 本段承担 conclusion 功能，收束并升华全文观点。它最终说明 romance 的价值不在虚假的 fantasy，而在它让读者相信 genuine connection 与 emotional chemistry 的可能性，从而完成评论者观念转变的落点。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: According to recent research, behavioral change involves physical changes in the brain. In the past decade, researchers have shown that when it comes to the duration of making a new behavior a deep-rooted habit there is not a simple answer. Even for the most productive and disciplined among us, undoing something that has become an automatic part of who we are takes more than an overnight effort. Once we've successfully made that change, we then have to make other adjustments to our lives to ensure that we continue to maintain it, which is often a whole other challenge in itself.
zh: 本段承担全文的引入功能，它先说明行为改变的 neurological basis 与现实难度，从而为后文提出 system 和五类 detrimental habits 提供必要的问题背景。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: At its core, success in changing and maintaining a behavior rarely occurs without the introduction of some sort of system. When there isn't the right framework in place, we face a greater likelihood of derailing our hard-earned progress. To ensure success in changing and maintaining a behavior, we should stay away from some detrimental habits.
zh: 本段是全文的 central bridge，它连接第一段的“改变很难”和后文的“五项建议”，并以 system 为全文提供统一的论证标准。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The first one to avoid is relying on willpower. Think about the last time you vowed to resist a temptation. Perhaps you didn't want to check your phone every 15 minutes, or you were determined not to reach for a chocolate bar at 3 p. m. Think about how difficult it must have been not to glance at your phone when it was within reach, or not to walk to the vending machine when your afternoon slump hit.
zh: 本段正式开启五个 detrimental habits 的论述，它先指出错误做法一，并通过日常 temptation 让读者感受到问题的普遍性，为下一段的理论解释作铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The research on whether we have finite or infinite willpower is inconclusive, but experts do generally agree that you can't change and sustain a habit if you rely on your willpower alone. The old military saying "You never rise to the occasion, you only sink to the level of training" also applies to behavior change. The idea is simple—you repeat something so many times that it becomes automatic.
zh: 本段深化了第一项建议的论证：它不仅说明 relying on willpower 为什么不可靠，还从习惯自动化的角度给出理论上的解决方向。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Think about what else you can change about your surrounding that makes it easier for you to perform this change on a daily basis. This is called your "cue." Basically, it's a trigger to perform that particular habit. If you don't want to reach for a sugary treat at 3 p. m. , have a box of herbal tea ready at your desk. When 3 p. m. comes around, that's your cue to pour yourself a cup of hot water and drink that tea, instead of walking to the vending machine.
zh: 本段将第一项建议转化为具体的 behavioral system：人不必硬扛诱惑，而可借助 cue 与替代行为降低执行好习惯的难度。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The second one to avoid is focusing on negative goals. Sometimes, it's not your process that lets you down, but the habit that you want to change in the first place. For starters, not eating chocolate to beat your afternoon slump is a harder goal than swapping chocolate for herbal tea when you reach the designated time. Your brain wants to find routines that have succeeded in the past and allow you to repeat those actions again in the future without having to think about them explicitly. However, this habit-learning system isn't so effective when it comes to learning not to do something. That's why rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place. Focus on actions you are going to take that will ultimately conflict with the behaviors you want to stop. When your attention is on doing something new, you give your habit system a chance to operate.
zh: 本段对应文章主旨中的第二项建议，它把目标设计从“戒除”转向“替换”，补充了 system 如何顺应大脑习惯机制。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The third one to avoid is using the same strategies in different circumstances. Because we are creatures of habit, it's natural to assume that when we do manage to adopt and sustain a desirable behavior, that same strategy will work when we want to make another behavior change. But that's not always the case. Sometimes, the system that got you to change one behavior might not work for another.
zh: 本段提出第三项错误习惯，起到承上启下作用：它先给出“策略不可照搬”的原则，下一段再用具体情境说明为何需要差异化 reinforcement。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Sometimes we become accustomed to relying on our guts when it comes to decision-making. This serves us well in certain situations, but can hinder us in others especially when we need to consider metrics and data, rather than letting our instinct override everything. For example, if you want to stop checking your email first thing in the morning, you might decide to substitute another activity in its place. But if you want to stop indulging in video games, simply deciding you will go for a run might not be as effective. You might need to introduce another reinforcement, such as meeting a friend and booking an exercise class together.
zh: 本段为第三项建议提供了细化说明，强调行为改变没有 universal formula，读者应按问题性质配置替代活动、数据判断或社会支持。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The fourth one to avoid is not forgiving ourselves for slipping up. Of course, even the best-laid plans fail sometimes. You might have stuck to your screen-free nighttime routine for five days, and then a big project landed on your desk and you found yourself in bed with your laptop before you went to sleep. Or you prepared meals on Sunday and stuck to eating healthy dinners at home, but by Friday you found yourself so exhausted and opted to order greasy takeout. Life happens and even if your behavior change is small, every single day can prove pretty inflexible, and at some point your luck may run out, even if just for a day. The perfectionist in you might be screaming to abandon your goals altogether, but try to see it in the bigger picture. Just because you might have temporarily strayed off course doesn't mean you can't start afresh the next day.
zh: 本段对应第四项建议，它防止读者陷入 all-or-nothing thinking，并用 self-compassion 保障行为改变在现实波动中仍能持续。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The final one to avoid is discounting small progress. There's a habit that many perfectionists tend to fall into when they try to establish a behavior change. They focus too much on the big goal and don't take the time to celebrate the small progress they make in the process. Your brain responds to rewards. The basal ganglia, the brain region linked to our performance of habits, is most active at the beginning of a behavior, when the habit is cued, and at the end, when it's rewarded. Say your goal is to run five miles three times a week, and this week you ran one mile on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Rather than focusing on how far you've gone toward your goal, think about how you can reward yourself for the progress you've made. It doesn't have to be big or expensive; it can be something as simple as making your favorite fruit juice after your run. Whatever your reward, it has to be more than just the activity itself to get you going.
zh: 本段完成五项 detrimental habits 的列举，并以 reward 机制说明为何庆祝小进步能增强持续性，直接呼应文章主旨中的 celebrate incremental achievements。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Initiating a new behavior usually seems like the hardest part of the process of change. However, people often fail to adequately prepare for maintaining it. One of the reasons for this is because we mistakenly believe the strategies we used to initiate the change will be equally effective in helping us continue the change. But they won't. Where changing a strongly deep-rooted habit requires changing our belief about that habit that penetrates deeply into our lives, continually manifesting that wisdom requires that we maintain a positive outlook. If our mood is low, the wisdom to behave differently seems to disappear and we go back to eating more and exercising less. The key, then, to maintaining new behaviors is to be happy! Which is why it's so hard to maintain new behaviors.
zh: 本段从前文五项具体错误提升到长期维持的心理条件，进一步补足文章主旨中 maintain behaviors 的维度，并揭示维持阶段的独特难题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Remember, overcoming the behavioral inertia that prevents us from implementing new changes, like eating a healthy diet or exercising, can benefit us in the long run and can improve our physical and mental health. No one was born with habits. They were all learned, and can all, therefore, be unlearned. The question is: how badly do you really want to change?
zh: 本段作为 conclusion，总结了全文反抗惯性、建立新习惯的长期价值，并以积极但带有追问的方式收束全文，鼓励读者将前述五项建议转化为实际 change。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: When someone asks us 'what do you do?' we nearly always reply with our occupation. Work, for many of us, is much more than a job. It is the defining aspect of our identity. For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves.
zh: 本段是全文的problem-setting，即提出问题的起点：人们过度依赖work来定义自己。它为后文解释失业为何会引发identity crisis，以及人为何应建立更开放的自我认知，提供了必要的逻辑前提。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.
zh: 本段承接第一段的“工作定义自我”，进一步说明这种观念的代价cost：一旦职业被迫改变，人会觉得连自我也失去了。它因此增强了全文论证的紧迫性，并为第三、四段提出更健康的identity观铺路。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community. We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work. The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work. Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. I myself have been a shop assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist. At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing. Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.
zh: 本段是全文的核心正向论证：它反驳了“我只是我的工作”这一狭隘假设，提出identity具有multiple和dynamic的本质。它也把论题从失业后的被动痛苦，推进到面对职业不确定性时应主动adapt的能力建设。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity. When we tell ourselves "I'm good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through" it can become part of our belief system. But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are. You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change. We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline. In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. Ultimately it is you who define who you are. You are only your job if you let it be so.
zh: 本段是全文的solution与conclusion：它回应第二段的identity crisis，也落实第三段的身份可变性。作者最终把identity的定义权交还给个人，完整收束文章主旨：人不应被job单独定义，而应主动建构更广阔的自我与career possibilities。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: A rainbow is a multi-colored, arc-shaped phenomenon that can appear in the sky. The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and dispersion of light through water droplets(小滴) present in the atmosphere. An observer may perceive a rainbow to be located either near or far away, but this phenomenon is not actually located at any specific spot. Instead, the appearance of a rainbow depends entirely upon the position of the observer in relation to the direction of light. In essence, a rainbow is an optical illusion.
zh: 本段承担全文的 opening function，它先回答“彩虹是什么”，并以 optical illusion 统领后文的颜色特征与形成原理。它尤其修正了“彩虹有固定位置”的直觉误解，使文章主旨中的 observer position 得到明确铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Rainbows present a spectrum made up of seven colors in a specific order. In fact, school children in many English-speaking countries are taught to remember the name "Roy G. Biv" as an aid for remembering the colors of a rainbow and their order. "Roy G. Biv" stands for: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. The outer edge of the rainbow arc is red, while the inner edge is violet.
zh: 本段从彩虹的视觉 appearance 切入，具体说明文章主旨中的 characteristic seven-color spectrum。它位于定义段与原理段之间，先让读者认识“看见什么”，再理解“为什么会看见这些颜色”。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: A rainbow is formed when light (generally sunlight) passes through water droplets hanging in the atmosphere. The light waves change direction as they pass through the water droplets, resulting in two processes: reflection and refraction(折射). When light reflects off a water droplet, it simply bounces back in the opposite direction from where it originates. When light refracts, it takes a different direction. Some individuals refer to refracted light as "bent light waves." A rainbow is formed because white light enters the water droplet, where it bends in several different directions. When these bent light waves reach the other side of the water droplet, they reflect back out of the droplet instead of completely passing through the water. Since the white light is separated inside of the water, the refracted light appears as separate colors to the human eye.
zh: 本段是全文的 scientific explanation，也是文章主旨中 how they form 的核心支撑。它把第一段提出的 light-water interaction 和第二段呈现的 seven colors 连接起来，从科学机制上解释彩虹为何会出现彩色弧形现象。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Phyllis Hartman knows what it's like to make one's way through the depths of office meeting hell. Managers at one of her former human resources jobs arranged so many meetings that attendees would fall asleep at the table or intentionally arrive late. With hours of her day blocked up with unnecessary meetings, she was often forced to make up her work during overtime. "I was actually working more hours than I probably would have needed to get the work done," says Hartman, who is founder and president of PGHR Consulting in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
zh: 本段以具体案例建立读者共鸣，使抽象的 MRS 议题先呈现为真实的 workplace pain，并为后文扩大问题范围作铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: She isn't alone in her frustration. Between 11 million and 55 million meetings are held each day in the United States, costing most organisations between 7% and 15% of their personnel budgets. Every week, employees spend about six hours in meetings, while the average manager meets for a staggering 23 hours.
zh: 本段承接 Hartman 的个案，以 statistics 证明问题具有普遍性和严重性，从而增强全文讨论 MRS 的必要性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: And though experts agree that traditional meetings are essential for making certain decisions and developing strategy, some employees view them as one of the most unnecessary parts of the workday. The result is not only hundreds of billions of wasted dollars, but an annoyance of what organisational psychologists call "meeting recovery syndrome (MRS)": time spent cooling off and regaining focus after a useless meeting. If you run to the office kitchen to get some relief with colleagues after a frustrating meeting, you're likely experiencing meeting recovery syndrome.
zh: 本段完成全文最关键的概念引入，把“会议浪费时间”的一般抱怨提升为 MRS 这一可被研究和解决的心理组织问题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Meeting recovery syndrome is a concept that should be familiar to almost anyone who has held a formal job. It isn't ground-breaking to say workers feel fatigued after a meeting, but only in recent decades have scientists deemed the condition worthy of further investigation. With its links to organisational efficiency and employee wellbeing, MRS has attracted the attention of psychologists aware of the need to understand its precise causes and cures.
zh: 本段为后文解释 MRS 的 causes 和 cures 建立学术合理性，说明研究该现象不仅有理论价值，也关系到效率与福祉。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Today, in so far as researchers can hypothesise, MRS is most easily understood as a slow renewal of finite mental and physical resources. When an employee sits through an ineffective meeting their brain power is essentially being drained away. Meetings drain vitality if they last too long, fail to engage employees or turn into one-sided lectures. The conservation of resources theory, originally proposed in 1989 by Dr Stevan Hobfoll, states that psychological stress occurs when a person's resources are threatened or lost. When resources are low, a person will shift into defence to conserve their remaining supply. In the case of office meetings, where some of employees' most valuable resources are their focus, alertness and motivation, this can mean an abrupt halt in productivity as they take time to recover.
zh: 本段从理论上回答 MRS “为什么发生”，使文章从现象描述进入因果阐释，也为下一段的任务转换困难提供基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: As humans, when we transition from one task to another on the job—say from sitting in a meeting to doing normal work—it takes an effortful cognitive switch. We must detach ourselves from the previous task and expend significant mental energy to move on. If we are already drained to dangerous levels, then making the mental switch to the next thing is extra tough. It's common to see people cyber-loafing after a frustrating meeting, going and getting coffee, interrupting a colleague and telling them about the meeting, and so on.
zh: 本段将资源耗竭理论落实到员工可观察的日常行为，具体说明 MRS 如何在会后直接侵蚀工作时间。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Each person's ability to recover from horrible meetings is different. Some can bounce back quickly, while others carry their fatigue until the end of the workday. Yet while no formal MRS studies are currently underway, one can loosely speculate on the length of an average employee's lag time. Switching tasks in a non-MRS condition takes about 10 to 15 minutes. With MRS, it may take as long as 45 minutes on average. It's even worse when a worker has several meetings that are separated by 30 minutes. "Not enough time to transition in a non-MRS situation to get anything done, and in an MRS situation, not quite enough time to recover for the next meeting," says researcher Joseph Allen. "Then, add the compounding of back-to-back bad meetings and we may have an epidemic on our hands."
zh: 本段进一步量化 MRS 的破坏力，特别揭示会议安排过密时，效率损失会从单次问题演变为组织性危机。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In an effort to combat the side effects of MRS, Allen, along with researcher Joseph Mroz and colleagues at the University of Nebraska-Omaha, published a study detailing the best ways to avoid common traps, including a concise checklist of do's and don'ts applicable to any workplace. Drawing from around 200 papers to compile their comprehensive list, Mroz and his team may now hold a remedy to the largely undefined problem of MRS.
zh: 本段是全文结构的重要转折点，它从分析 MRS 的危害与机制，过渡到介绍可操作的应对策略。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Mroz says a good place to start is asking ourselves if our meetings are even necessary in the first place. If all that's on the agenda is a quick catch-up, or some non-urgent information sharing, it may better suit the group to send around an email instead. "The second thing I would always recommend is keep the meeting as small as possible," says Mroz. "If they don't actually have some kind of immediate input, then they can follow up later. They don't need to be sitting in this hour-long meeting." Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to more employee engagement in the meetings they do attend, which experts agree is a proven remedy for MRS.
zh: 本段给出最直接的组织层面方案：从会议是否召开及谁该参加两方面减少无效消耗，回应了前文的会议过载问题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Employees also feel taxed when they are invited together to meetings that don't inspire participation, says Cliff Scott, professor of organisational science. It takes precious time for them to vent their emotions, complain and try to regain focus after a pointless meeting—one of the main traps of MRS. Over time as employees find themselves tied up in more and more unnecessary meetings—and thus dealing with increasing lag times from MRS—the waste of workday hours can feel insulting.
zh: 本段补充说明 MRS 不只是认知资源问题，也包含员工被忽视后的情绪成本，从而深化了无效会议危害的层次。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Despite the relative scarcity of research behind the subject, Hartman has taught herself many of the same tricks suggested in Mroz's study, and has come a long way since her days of being stuck with unnecessary meetings. The people she invites to meetings today include not just the essential employees, but also representatives from every department that might have a stake in the issue at hand. Managers like her, who seek input even from non-experts to shape their decisions, can find greater support and cooperation from their workforce, she says.
zh: 本段形成首尾呼应：开头的受害者 Hartman 在此成为实践者，证明前述改善会议的理念能够转化为更强的员工支持与合作。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: If an organisation were to apply all 22 suggestions from Mroz and Allen's findings, the most noticeable difference would be a stark decrease in the total number of meetings on the schedule, Mroz says. Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to increased productivity, which is the ultimate objective of convening a meeting. While none of the counter-MRS ideas have been tested empirically yet, Allen says one trick with promise is for employees to identify things that quickly change their mood from negative to positive. As simple as it sounds, finding a personal happy place, going there and then coming straight back to work might be key to facilitating recovery.
zh: 本段进一步展示 MRS 对策的预期效果，并补充会后即时恢复的个人策略，使解决方案兼具组织和个人两个维度。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Leaders should also see themselves as "stewards of everyone else's valuable time", adds Steven Rogelberg, author of The Surprising Science of Meetings. Having the skills to foresee potential traps and treat employees' endurance with care allows leaders to provide effective short-term deterrents to MRS.
zh: 本段将 MRS 的治理责任明确落在领导者身上，说明有效会议并非仅靠员工自我恢复，而需要管理者的前瞻安排。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Most important, however, is for organisations to awaken to the concept of meetings being flexible, says Allen. By reshaping the way they prioritise employees' time, companies can eliminate the very sources of MRS in their tracks.
zh: 本段收束全文，提出最根本的组织变革方向：只有重新优先考虑 employees' time，才能从根源上消除 MRS，而非仅处理其后果。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Variability is crucially important for learning new skills. Consider learning how to serve in tennis. Should you always practise serving from the exactly same location on the court, aiming at the same spot? Although practising in more variable conditions will be slower at first, it will likely make you a better tennis player in the end. This is because variability leads to better generalisation of what is learned.
zh: 本段承担全文的引入功能，先提出 variability improves generalisation 的总论点。后文将从跨领域证据、研究发现、作用机制和现实影响等方面，逐步解释并扩展这一核心观点。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: This principle is found in many domains, including speech perception and learning categories. For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.
zh: 本段为文章主旨提供跨领域的初步证据，说明 variability 的作用具有 general applicability。它把第一段的运动学习结论延伸到语言感知和概念分类，使文章论证范围更广。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: "There are over ten different names for this basic principle," says Limor Raviv, the senior investigator of a recent study. "Learning from less variable input is often fast, but may fail to generalise to new stimuli."
zh: 本段从反面论证文章主旨，指出低变异输入虽有效率优势，却可能牺牲 generalisation。它进一步解释了为什么第一段所说的“初期较慢”并不意味着多样化练习较差。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: To identify key patterns and understand the underlying principles of variability effects, Raviv and her colleagues reviewed over 150 studies on variability and generalisation across fields, including computer science, linguistics, categorisation, visual perception and formal education.
zh: 本段由一般原理转入学术研究，为后文的发现建立 evidence base。150 多项 studies 和跨领域范围增强了文章关于 variability 的论证可信度与普遍性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The researchers discovered that, across studies, the term variability can refer to at least four different kinds of variability, such as set size and scheduling. "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.
zh: 本段细化了文章主旨中的 variability 概念，并指出当前研究的 unresolved question。它避免读者把“多样性有效”简单化，也为后续研究提供了明确方向。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The impact of variability depends on whether it is relevant to the task or not. But according to the 'Mr. Miyagi principle', practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills.
zh: 本段为文章主旨增加条件性，说明 variability 的收益不是机械发生的。它促使读者进一步思考：哪些变化真正有助于学习，以及技能间为何会发生 transfer。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But why does variability impact learning and generalisation? One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not.
zh: 本段开始解释 variability improves generalisation 的内在原因。通过帮助学习者筛选 relevant information，它为前文的学习迁移效果提供了第一个理论支撑。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations. This is because variability will represent the real world better, including atypical(非典型的) examples.
zh: 本段提供第二种机制解释，并直接呼应全文的 generalisation 主题。它说明学习者接触 atypical examples 后，形成的规则更接近真实世界的复杂性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.
zh: 本段补充第三个理论维度，即认知记忆机制。至此，文章从特征筛选、现实表征和 memory reconstruction 三方面，共同解释 variability 的学习价值。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: "Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life. Beyond affecting the way we learn language, motor skills, and categories, it even has an impact on our social lives," explains Raviv. "For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community. Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory."
zh: 本段提升了文章主旨的现实意义，说明 variability 并非仅是课堂或实验室中的学习问题。它把这一原则延伸到 social cognition，使读者认识到早期经验多样性可能影响日常社会能力。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: "We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv. "Our paper raises a lot of open questions. Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system?"
zh: 本段完成全文收束，并把文章主旨从已有发现推向未来研究。它表明 variability 的影响范围可能超出学习与大脑，为读者留下进一步探究的科学问题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: On a small fruit farm near the Straits of Malacca, Lim Kok Ann is down to just one tree growing kedondong, a crunchy, sour berry that Malaysians mostly use in pickles(腌菜) and salads. "It's not very well-known," says the 45-year-old, who is instead focusing on longan(龙眼) berries and pineapples, which have bigger markets. "We have to grow what is profitable," he says.
zh: 本段用一个真实的 local example 制造问题意识，为后文科研人员如何复兴被忽视作物埋下了叙事伏笔。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But less than an hour away in the Malaysian countryside, inside three giant, silver domes, scientists are trying to change the future of food. They're pushing the boundaries of what humans eat by growing and processing so-called "alternative" crops—such as kedondong. At the headquarters of global research centre Crops For the Future (CFF) this particular under-used fruit has been turned into a sugar-free juice, high in vitamin C and getting top marks in sensory evaluations. "Anything you see here is a forgotten crop," says Sayed Azam-Ali of the abundant plants weaving through the gardens of CFF outside Malaysia's capital Kuala Lumpur.
zh: 本段提出文章的主要解决者 CFF，并与首段的弃种现象形成 contrast，表明 forgotten crops 并非没有价值，而是缺少开发。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Prof Azam-Ali explains that just four crops—wheat, maize, rice and soybean—provide two-thirds of the world's food supply. "We're dependent on these four," he says. "But actually there're 7,000 crops we've been farming for thousands of years. We ignore all of those." Researchers are trying to unlock the potential of these ignored crops—plants they describe as forgotten, under-used or "alternative" as they are displaced by increasingly uniform diets fuelled by processed ingredients from the major crops.
zh: 本段从个别作物上升到 global food system，明确解释了为什么 forgotten crops 值得被关注。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: It's a timely quest. The food sector is already responsible for nearly a third of global greenhouse gas emissions. By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion. Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions.
zh: 本段承担 problem-setting 功能，把 forgotten crops 的讨论放进全球 climate 和 food demand 的宏大背景中。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Forgotten crops hold key answers. By investing in neglected local plants, countries can reduce their reliance on imported crops and their carbon-heavy supply chains. Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate also boosts food security at a time warming climates threaten existing crops. On top of that forgotten crops are among the most climate-resilient(具有气候韧性的) and nutritious, argues Azam-Ali. His summary is plain: "Dietary diversification is critical to the future of humanity."
zh: 本段是全文的核心论证段，正面回答 forgotten crops 为什么可能成为 future of food。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Food security experts agree. "There is no food insecurity in the world, there is food ignorance," says Cecilia Tortajada, a senior research fellow at the Institute of Water Policy at the National University of Singapore. "Whenever we have native crops we tend to disregard them as if they were not valuable but they are," she adds.
zh: 本段以专家背书强化第五段的观点，并指出推广难点不仅是资源不足，更是认知偏见。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Azam-Ali knows that scepticism firsthand. He came across alternative crops in the 1980s through the work of women farmers he met in Niger. The then-PhD student remembers marvelling at the crops they grew in their backyards, without the benefits of technology, to feed their families when the big crops failed. He saw a tremendous opportunity to build alternative food systems. But "the resistance was enormous," he recalls.
zh: 本段补充倡导者的个人背景，使文章从抽象研究转为有历史感的人物叙事，同时引出后文的市场难题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Undeterred, he ploughed on. Project after project helped prove these crops were viable in different environments as alternatives to the staple ones. But the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained. "That's the critical thing," he says. In one of the centre's domes, food technologist Tan Xinlin uses powdered moringa(辣木) leaves in place of some wheat flour to bake a cake lower in gluten(谷胶) and higher in nutrients. Tan's job is to create recipes with these still-unfamiliar ingredients that will appeal to both local and international tastes. In recent years she has used some of the forgotten crops grown at CFF, such as moringa and bambara groundnut, to make everything from instant soup to Indian snacks. "I try to modernise forgotten crops instead of using old recipes." says Tan, who is also a trained chef. It's a strategy to appeal to the world's growing middle classes who are increasingly turning to the fast and processed food industries. It's also a way to help counter perceptions of local crops as "old or poor people's food" or as inferior "women's crops", adds Tan.
zh: 本段将论证推进到 commercialization，说明 forgotten crops 的复兴必须跨越从实验田到消费市场的关键一步。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The roots of these connotations about local foods can run deep. The bambara groundnut, a protein-rich native crop of sub-Saharan Africa that is also grown in parts of southeast Asia, can trace its marginalisation to colonial rule. "African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it," says Azam-Ali. "Colonial powers said you can't grow that because there's no oil. We can't get a market for it." But today the bambara murukku is one of CFF's best reviewed foods and they are aiming to get it into grocery stores, pointing to the success of crops like quinoa to potential investors. Some 30 years ago, quinoa was virtually unheard of outside its native mountains in Bolivia and Peru. Today the nutritious grain is found on the menus of lavish restaurants across the world.
zh: 本段深化了第八段的社会偏见问题，并以 quinoa 为先例增强投资者和读者对商业化前景的信心。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Measuring crops by nutrition instead of yield is at the heart of the forgotten foods enterprise. Ever since the "green revolution" of the 1960s, high-yielding crops have dominated modern agriculture. That was in part a crucial response to devastating famines at a time when the world needed to increase its food supply. Today "nutrition is becoming a time bomb", says Azam-Ali, as growing carbon dioxide levels strip crops of their minerals. Instead of bio-fortifying major crops we should be investing in those forgotten crops that are already more nutritious, he asserts.
zh: 本段为 forgotten crops 增加营养学维度，使全文的论证从环境与安全进一步扩展到 human health。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In the bowels of CFF's third dome, lab manager Gomathy Sethuraman opens a window into the centre's "crown jewels", revealing vines of winged beans growing under a bright yellow light. It's one of multiple chambers where scientists are studying the impact of higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels on the nutritional make-up of alternative crops. This research is "the game changer", says Azam-Ali, ensuring that "future crops" are also the healthiest ones in warmer climates.
zh: 本段提供科学研究证据，具体支撑文章关于 forgotten crops 具有 climate resilience 和 nutritional value 的中心论断。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: There is a growing global momentum around forgotten foods, says Danielle Nierenberg, president of Food Tank, a US-based think tank. Other than CFF, which bills itself as the world's first research centre dedicated solely to under-utilised crops, there are other key groups championing agricultural diversity including Crop Trust, Slow Food, Icrisat and Bioversity International. Add to that more middle-income consumers searching for nutritious foods and others eager to try the unprocessed foods their grandparents once ate, she says.
zh: 本段展现积极前景，说明 forgotten foods 的推广已有研究机构、社会组织和市场需求的共同支撑。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But the rising interest in forgotten foods in some quarters is overtaken by the global spread of Western-style diets heavy in sugar, fat and processed foods in others.
zh: 本段扭转第十二段的乐观语气，提醒读者推广 forgotten foods 仍面对强劲的全球化饮食阻力。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: A key obstacle to promoting fading local crops in Malaysia, for example, is "the obsession with imported products", says Jenifer Kuah, co-founder of a restaurant that champions locally-sourced food in an affluent suburb of Kuala Lumpur. Customers at Sitka, regarded as a pioneer in the country's small farm-to-table dining scene, still seek foreign ingredients as a "status symbol", she says.
zh: 本段将前段的宏观饮食冲突落实到 Malaysia 的消费现实，具体说明市场和文化偏见为何难以改变。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The argument for forgotten foods feels intuitive. Some analysts say it is in fact inevitable. "Climate change is going to mean almost certainly tastes are going to be forced to change," says Tim Lang, professor of food policy at City, University of London. We "have to get used to eating other crops" as yields of staple crops fall, he says.
zh: 本段以 climate-driven necessity 收束全文，强化文章最终立场：面对主粮风险，人类必须逐渐接受 other crops。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years. But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.
zh: 本段承担 introduction 的功能，它先搭建“线下反抗、线上强化”的矛盾框架；这一框架为后文解释 social media 如何制造并强化新审美标准作了铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel. In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don't correspond to the so-called ideal. All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda, have become "legitimate". At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws.
zh: 本段具体展开了线下或现实层面的 positive movement，并暂时呈现较乐观的变化；它与后文 digital beauty ideal 的负面机制构成鲜明 contrast，从而增强文章的批判力度。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses. One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the "cyborg look", which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050.
zh: 本段从前文的社会反抗转入 technology 的塑形作用，首次说明数字审美并非自然形成；它为下文 Instagram face 取代 cyborg look 埋下了发展线索。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The cyborg look spread rapidly. Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.
zh: 本段完成了从旧式 digital trend 到当下 Instagram ideal 的转换；它把论证对象锁定为社交平台上的主流“脸”，使后文对互动机制和滤镜机制的分析更具体。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process. The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified(游戏化的) interaction offered by the social media platforms—the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share.
zh: 本段是全文论证的关键 mechanism，它解释 social media 为什么能有效塑造审美：平台通过主动互动让用户自我参与、自我强化；这直接呼应文章主旨中的 gamified interactions。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal such as editing the image, choosing the ideal filter, the right background.
zh: 本段承接 第5段，展示从心理认同到实际操作的第二步；用户先接受标准，再用 filters 和 editing 改造照片，这使平台审美从观念转化为可见的日常行为。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: A survey conducted in the United States revealed that more than 50% filter the images before posting them. And you will not be surprised to hear that the majority of them are women. One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.
zh: 本段把前文的修图行为推进到心理层面：filtering 不再只是外貌加工，而会改变用户看待自己的方式；它直接对应文章主旨中的 obsessive image editing 和 self-objectification。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The effect of the filters is already far beyond amiable amusement. The filters and the entire game played on the networks affect the mental health of the users. According to a study, apps like Instagram, Snapchat and FaceTune allow users to achieve a level of perfection that was previously only observed in beauty magazines.
zh: 本段进一步升级论证后果，从 第7段 的 self-objectification 推进到 mental health damage；它为末段提出 mental health care 的解决方向提供了直接依据。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Even though humanity has always cherished beauty, in the last decade our obsession with looks has reached an unprecedented peak. The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care.
zh: 本段作为 conclusion，回收全文的论证链：social media 制造 impossible ideal，用户因此陷入前所未有的外貌焦虑，最终产生 mental health problem；它也完整落实了文章主旨中的“心理干预优于美容解决”。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Ever been talking about something important with someone you care about and found the discussion frustrating instead of fruitful? Negative energy can then cast a shadow over your efforts to build a shared understanding.
zh: 本段承担 introduction 功能，它先提出重要谈话为何会变得 frustrating，为后文说明 collaborative dialogue 所需条件作铺垫。虽然全文重点最终落到 symmetry，但这一段先建立了“有效对话会受情绪破坏”的总问题背景。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In fact collaborative problem-solving conversations require skills. Strong listening skills are essential. Sprinkling in positivity via appreciation, affectionate smiles, and warm comments helps. So does the essential ability to keep your emotional tone in the calm zone. If the tone of a dialogue heats up and anger erupts, the dialogue flips from collaborative to adversarial, and progress is likely to come to an immediate halt.
zh: 本段在首段的问题背景之后，先概述 effective dialogue 的普遍条件。它既回应了 negative energy 的危害，也为下一段用 In addition 引出更具体、更核心的 symmetry 条件建立逻辑台阶。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In addition, effective dialogue generally has another important characteristic: symmetry.
zh: 本段是全文的 pivot，即论述重心的转折点。它把前文对有效沟通的宽泛讨论聚焦到 symmetry，并自然引领第4至第6段分别解释不对称的不同表现。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Symmetry in dialogue refers to the balance of how much each partner talks. Are you each getting equal airtime? When one participant does most of the talking, this asymmetry or lack of balance tends to become annoying to one or both of you. The silent partner typically tires of only listening, while the talker can feel overburdened. Usually, both would prefer more equal give and take.
zh: 本段开始具体阐释 symmetry 的第一个维度，即 airtime 的均衡。它把第3段的抽象概念落地，并以双方的不满证明：发言时间失衡会削弱 productive conversation。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Different rates of speech and levels of voice volume can erode symmetry as well. The faster or louder partner can easily begin taking up more airtime. The slower-talking or softer-voiced one can have trouble getting the floor.
zh: 本段进一步说明，不平等发言并不总是源于主观抢话，也可能来自 speed 和 volume 的自然差异。它拓宽了文章对 asymmetry 成因的解释，使读者能识别更隐蔽的沟通障碍。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Conversations also lose balance when one partner's opinions count more than the other's. One person's input may carry more sway because their style of expression is more vigorous. One viewpoint may tend to get lost because it is expressed more tentatively.
zh: 本段完成了对 symmetry 的更深层界定：真正的平衡不仅是都能开口，更是每个人的 input 都能产生相近的影响。它与文章主旨中的 balanced influence 直接对应，也增强了全文论证的深度。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: If either partner fairly consistently predominates or evaporates, modifying the pattern will be helpful. The dialogue will feel more productive, and at the same time, the relationship overall is likely to feel more positive.
zh: 本段是全文的 conclusion，它回应前文所有 airtime、speech style 和 opinion weight 的失衡现象，并给出总解决方向：恢复 symmetry。它最终证明，平衡参与不仅提升对话效率，也能改善双方的 relationship quality。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Blue moons, rose moons, supermoons. For some reason all the websites seem to think you really want to know all about these moons. "Catch This Weekend's AMAZING SUPERMOON," one headline will announce. "The Supermoon Isn't Actually A Big Deal And You're All Ruining Astronomy," another will complain.
zh: 本段以媒体话语作为 opening hook，把普通月相现象被过度包装的问题推到读者面前，从而自然引出后文的科学解释与辟谣。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The latest example is the super blood wolf moon eclipse which sounds like the name of an emotional song I would have performed a modern dance routine to in 9th grade, but is, in fact, an astronomical event set to occur on January 20. As we'll explain below, there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon, and it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky or anything wild like that. We get these super lunar events by smashing together all the qualifiers we've historically used to keep track of full moons throughout the year, and in the age of the internet we can get a little too enthusiastic.
zh: 本段直接提出全文的 central claim：戏剧化名称并不等于罕见或神秘的事实，后续各段将逐一拆解 super、blood、blue 和 wolf 等限定词。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Consider this your go-to resource for all moon-gazing news. Here's what you need to know about the latest lunar event.
zh: 本段充当 bridge，把前两段的媒体炒作话题转入后文的科普说明，使文章从提出问题进入逐项解答。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Look, it's okay if you don't know. There are probably loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not.
zh: 本段把抽象的天文话题转化为读者真实的疑问，增强科普文章的针对性，并引出下一段对月相成因的基础讲解。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The moon orbits Earth, and it's tidally locked—that means it always shows us the same face, instead of spinning around like our planet does. That's why you can always see the man on the moon (or the moon rabbit, depending on your cultural preferences) even as it spins around us. But while the moon is big and bright in the sky when it's full, that's only because it's reflecting light from the sun. But the moon is always moving, so it's getting hit with sunlight at different angles. It's invisible to us during the new moon, because our satellite is parked right between us and the sun; the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow. A full moon happens when the earth is right between the sun and the moon, so sunlight hits the part we can see. And all the other phases are just the transition from one of those extremes to the other.
zh: 本段提供全文最基础的 scientific foundation，使读者先理解普通月相，才能进一步理解满月、血月和超级月亮等特殊称谓。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth, because its orbit isn't perfectly circular. We call the closest point perigee(近地点), and the most distant point is apogee(远地点). 2018's closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January, and the difference was about 30,000 miles.
zh: 本段为 supermoon 的形成补上关键条件，即月地距离的周期性变化；它承接基础月相知识，并为下一段的“超级”解释蓄势。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The reason you care about this ordinary change in distance is that it turns a moon super. When a full moon happens close to perigee, it's going to look a bit bigger. Honestly, the difference is not that profound, but if you're in a position to photograph the supermoon next to something that shows the slight increase in scale, it can look pretty cool. January's super blood wolf moon eclipse is super because the date lines up with the closest the moon will get to us during January, but the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year until February's supermoon, which you can expect plenty of undue excitement over.
zh: 本段完成对 super 的科学拆解，并以“差别不大”的判断具体落实全文反对 sensationalism 的总体主旨。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Blood moons only occur during total lunar eclipses (which can happen a few times a year in any given location). When the moon slips through our shadow, we give it a reddish coloring. The moon can also look orange whenever it's rising or setting, or if it hangs low in the horizon all night—the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there, which scatters more blue light away. But you'll probably only see that deep, sinister red during an eclipse.
zh: 本段拆解 blood 一词的真实天文含义，说明所谓“鲜血般的月亮”只是可预测的月全食光学效果，而非神秘征兆。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: A lot of headlines about moons are just ridiculous (you do not need to be particularly excited about a blue moon, it just looks like a regular full moon), but you should definitely roll out of bed to look at a blood moon if one is going to be visible in your region, even though they're just lunar eclipses and not evidence of bloody battles between the sky gods.
zh: 本段防止文章的辟谣立场走向“毫无价值”的极端，表明科学解释并不排斥欣赏自然奇观，增强了论述的平衡性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In March of 2018, we had our second "blue moon" of the year, to much acclaim. And while that's not necessarily special in an oh-gosh-get-out-and-look-at-it way, it's certainly special: a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moons fall in the same calendar month, and we hadn't previously had two in one year since 1999. We won't have it happen again until 2037. Astronomer David Chapman explained that this is merely a peculiarity of our calendar; once we stopped doing things based on the moon and started trying to follow the sun and the seasons, we stopped having one reliable full moon per month. The moon cycle is 29.53 days long on average, so in most months we still end up with a single new moon and a single full one. But every once in a while, one month steals a full moon from another. In 2018 (and in 1999, and again in 2037) both January and March stacked full moons on the first and last nights of the month, leaving February in the dark.
zh: 本段系统解释 blue 的第一层含义，进一步证明耸动名称往往来自人类计时系统，而不是月球本身突然出现异常。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Getting two blue moons a year is rare, but we have individual blue moons every few years. Also, fun fact: not actually blue. A moon can indeed take on a moody blue color, but this only happens when particles of just the right size disperse through the sky—and it has nothing to do with the moon's status as "blue". Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires can do the trick, but it doesn't happen often, and the stars would certainly have to align for two such rare instances to occur at once.
zh: 本段深化对 blue moon 的去神秘化：它不仅在定义上是日历现象，在颜色上也与名称不符，强化全文纠正误解的目的。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: You may have heard that the super special second blue moon of 2018 was also a Paschal moon. This is true! That just means it was the first full moon of spring, which is often used to determine the date of Easter Sunday. All of this is just calendar nonsense and we refuse to go into it further.
zh: 本段补充又一个附加标签，说明公众所谓“超级特殊”的组合事件常由多个 calendar categories 叠加，而非由罕见天文异象构成。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Sometimes you'll see a headline that promises a moon with so many qualifiers it makes your head spin. A super blue blood worm moon, perhaps? Or a super blood wolf moon? Lots of websites will tell you that "wolf moon" is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in "Native American" cultures, which is kind of a weird thing to claim given that there are 573 registered Tribal Nations in the US alone today, not to mention historically. The idea that hungry, howling wolves were such a universal constant in January that all of North America with its different cultures, geographies, and languages spontaneously came up with the same nickname is illogical.
zh: 本段把文章的批判范围从科学夸张扩展到文化简化，表明媒体拼接月亮标签时，不仅可能误导天文事实，也可能误读文化传统。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Many cultures have traditional names for the full moon in a given month or season, so there's quite a list to draw from if you're trying to really juice up a story on a slightly-bigger-than-average view of the moon. But these are all based on human calendars and activities and folklore; you will not go outside and see a pink moon in April, though I wish it were so.
zh: 本段以总括性的方式结束文章：无论是 wolf、pink 还是其他名称，大多是人类赋予的 cultural labels，从最终层面呼应全文反对神秘化和夸张化的主旨。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者)", are rarely questioned. They've become so embedded in our consciousness that people think it's absurd to think otherwise. It might be useful, however, to at least push back on this assumption because people evaluate environment, situations, and people aesthetically. We may find that we still believe it is correct, but we may also find that there is a lot more to the situation than you suppose.
zh: 作为 introduction，本段建立全文争论对象：美是否仅由个人眼光决定。它为后文引入 study、解释自然物与人工制品的差异，并最终提出 objective principles 作好了逻辑铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition. The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.
zh: 本段以研究结果直接削弱“美完全因人而异”的绝对说法。既然许多人对自然物有 shared taste，就说明审美判断中可能存在超越个体偏好的共同因素。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art. The hypothesis is the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.
zh: 本段把“存在共同审美”推进为“共同审美可能有共同基础”。其中 proportion 和 symmetry 为文章第七至九段提出 universal principles of beauty 提供了早期依据。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences. Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop. Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.
zh: 本段补充说明自然物为何更容易形成审美共识。即使这种偏好部分来自 learned experience，只要人类共享类似的生存条件，审美仍可能具有相对客观、普遍的基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.
zh: 本段回应潜在反驳：既然人们对艺术和建筑意见不一，美是否仍然主观？作者的回答是，这种分歧可以由 exposure 的不一致解释，因此不能据此否定共同审美原则。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: It's possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has to do more with elements of style, rather than "behavioral consequences".
zh: 本段继续限定人工制品审美分歧的来源。它为第九段铺路：艺术家和建筑师会以 unique ways 运用普遍原则，而不同风格的具体实现未必能获得 universal appeal。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw. It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations. I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.
zh: 这是全文的论证核心和立场落点。前六段的研究发现与可能解释，在本段被提升为哲学结论：美不只是“in the eye of the beholder”，还可能受客观原则支配。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.
zh: 本段为第七段的 objective principles 提供直观论据。自然物中可重复出现的 radiance 等特征，使“不同人可能共享某些审美依据”的论断显得更具体、更可信。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Possible universal principles of beauty—such as proportion, fittingness, radiance, and others—are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments. When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.
zh: 本段是全文最重要的逻辑调和环节。它解释了为什么作者既能承认艺术和建筑存在个体、文化差异，又能坚持美背后可能存在 universal principles，从而使中心论点更严密。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: This is why it's important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts because it opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty. And it is always good to question our assumptions.
zh: 本段将前文的哲学讨论转化为 practical value。作者并未因为存在某些 objective principles 而否定文化多样性，反而强调应通过 diverse cultures 理解美的不同表达，并保持对自身判断的反思。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: About 23% of the global population lives in absolute poverty. In developing countries there is a low life expectancy, a high infant mortality rate, high levels of unemployment and illiteracy, nutritional levels below acceptable standards and widespread disease with very little or poor quality medical assistance. Others live incredibly wealthy and luxurious lives and so the wealth is distributed in a very unequal manner. These are the central problems to questions of charity though charity also includes many other areas such as assisting the elderly.
zh: 本段为全文提供了事实基础：若不存在 widespread poverty 和 extreme inequality，后文关于捐赠责任的 moral argument 就缺少紧迫性。它把抽象的 charity 置于真实的人类困境中，从而为文章主旨中的“有能力者应帮助有需要者”建立 problem-based justification。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: We all applaud when very rich people pledge to give away most of their billions, but they are usually left with millions to pass on, still much more than most people would expect to earn in their lifetime. Even comparatively moderate salaries in the west are very high when compared globally. Someone on £ 20,000 could easily afford to give away £ 2,000 per year and still have plenty to live on plus some luxuries.
zh: 本段承接首段的贫困背景，进一步回答“谁应当帮助、为什么能够帮助”这一问题。它通过 affordability 削弱“捐赠会损害自身生活”的潜在反驳，为全文将 charity 提升为 moral obligation 提供关键的能力前提：有经济余裕者并非无力承担。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Most people agree that giving to charity is morally praiseworthy but charitable behaviour tends to be regarded as above and beyond the call of duty. Some argue, however, that charitable behaviour is morally required. This means that to fail to behave charitably would be wrong. The majority of arguments in this vein refer to giving aid to poorer nations but they may also refer to giving time within one's immediate community. Arguments tend to place different requirements on people in different income brackets and exclude entirely people who are merely making ends meet. Some argue that people should all contribute a certain percentage of their earnings. I will group together all those arguments that place a moral requirement on people to give to charity, despite the fact that there is wide disagreement as to the extent of that moral requirement.
zh: 本段把前两段的现实背景与经济能力，正式转化为伦理结论：面对贫困且具备余力时，giving 不应只是 optional virtue，而可能是 required duty。它既明确文章主旨，也预先界定责任的弹性边界，避免把论点误读为要求所有人不计代价地捐赠。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Trade is one of the policy areas where the hostility that exists between populists(民粹主义者) and classical liberals is most visible. Free-traders point to the undeniable good that tariff-free trade has done for consumers across the world and to the observable alleviation of poverty in corners of the world where previously closed markets have been opened up. Protectionists point to the domestic producers who've paid the price for this globalized economy in the form of lost livelihoods and hollowed-out communities.
zh: 本段为全文建立了 policy debate 的表层矛盾：自由贸易有明显 benefits，但也造成具体伤害；后文则会进一步追问，为什么这种矛盾在政治上尤其难以化解。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The ongoing conservative civil war often degenerates into content-free tribal warfare, but trade is a rare exception. There are substantial, thought-out policy proposals on both sides of the argument.
zh: 本段承接第一段的立场冲突，并把贸易定位为一个值得认真处理的议题；它为下一段提出“真正理解、有效对话”的可能性作铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Consequently, trade as a topic of discussion provides an opportunity for liberals and populists to have a real meeting of minds. Fruitful debates might actually take place in this area, as opposed to the familiar ritual we've become accustomed to of condemnation met with counter-condemnation.
zh: 本段将前文的“可讨论性”提升为“可沟通性”，但作者随后会反转视角，指出阻碍这种沟通的深层问题并不是简单的经济利益。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Strange as it might sound, the problem with trade in the modern world isn't a matter of dollars and cents. It's a matter of false consciousness. This observation is bound to set Marxist alarm bells ringing in the minds of some readers, but it was first made by Alexis de Tocqueville in 1840.
zh: 这是全文最关键的理论转轴：作者开始解释自由贸易为何难以赢得情感和政治支持，并把答案定位为人们未能意识到自己的 global dependence。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Tracking the economic development of mankind from primitive to modern societies, Tocqueville observed a paradox unfolding over the centuries as economic realities and human experience of those realities strayed further and further from each other. In primitive societies, he notes, the division of labor was as yet undeveloped for the most part, requiring each person, family, or tribe to be relatively independent when it came to meeting their own basic material needs. Men built their own dwellings, farmed their own land, tended to their own livestock. This is not to deny that basic forms of trade took place, but, for the most part, our primitive ancestors lived fairly self-reliant, if crushingly poor, lives.
zh: 本段提供比较的第一端，即原始人的经济现实；后文会说明，尽管他们较为自给，却因为面对面生活而更能感知与他人的联系。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: However, the exclusively local and face-to-face nature of economic and political organization in the ancient and prehistoric worlds constantly impressed upon these primitive peoples the uncontrollable reality of others and their needs. As Tocqueville notes, "as soon as a man begins to deal with common affairs in public, he begins to perceive that he is not so independent of his fellow men as he had first imagined, and that in order to obtain their support he must often lend them his cooperation."
zh: 本段补足了原始社会的另一面：经济上较独立，意识上却更明白人与人的联系；这正为下一段的现代 paradox 蓄势。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示
