Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we've come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.
zh: 本段将宏观的公平诉求落实到教育实践，直接呼应文章主旨中 truthful education 的关键路径。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.
zh: 本段提供了一个可操作的教育改革方案，使文章从价值倡议进一步落到 educator diversity 的制度建设。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements. A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before". But reports of increased polarization shouldn't persuade us to look away from one another. Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.
zh: 本段回应了改革为何艰难，同时强调分裂不是放弃对话的理由，从而巩固全文的 dialogue 与 collective action 立场。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: We are not, as some would suggest, living in a "post-racial society". We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity. Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us. But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.
zh: 本段强化全文最核心的价值判断：不承认种族不平等就无法消除它，并以未来世代增加了改革的紧迫性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."
zh: 本段收束全文，将前文的真相、教育、公平与反分裂主张汇聚为集体行动，最终呼应 King 关于和平与良知社会的理想。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in. However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.
zh: 本段作为 introduction，先建立“友谊珍贵”与“成功导致失友”之间的 tension，为全文反对这种 normalized sacrifice 奠定论题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships. As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.
zh: 本段承接首段，进一步解释友谊为何被放弃，同时揭示这种放弃并非完全无奈，而带有 self-justification 的文化心理。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track. We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.
zh: 本段是全文的 central claim，直接提出应珍视 connections，并首次点出 radical individual freedom 是需要反思的思想根源。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective. It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans.
zh: 本段为后文批评个人成就崇拜提供理论框架，使“失去朋友”不再只是个人选择，而被放入 individualism 与 collectivism 的价值冲突中。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture. Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.
zh: 本段把前文定义的 radical individualism 落实为普遍社会文化，说明人们轻视友谊的深层原因是对个人 achievement 的集体推崇。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: As a society, we idolize the concept of "losing friends on the road to success". I remember hearing in high school, "Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college. That's all that will matter in the long run," a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories, and it's embedded in the way we see growth. Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.
zh: 本段是全文最主要的 evidence 段，通过个人记忆和社会实例证明：牺牲关系并非自然规律，而是被 success narrative 主动塑造的观念。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives. We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades. In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.
zh: 本段总结前文的社会批评，进一步指出问题的严重后果：人们不仅失去朋友，还因成就标准的压力而对这种失去变得麻木。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.
zh: 本段进入 solution 阶段，纠正“独自成功更高贵”的错误假设，并从价值层面强调 friendships 对人生的不可替代性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.
zh: 本段完成全文 conclusion，将前面的批评转化为可执行的建议，并重申文章主旨：面对个人主义社会，关系的支持与爱比最终结果更值得守护。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: We humans love to believe we are special, but science and technology have repeatedly proved this conviction wrong. People once thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things.
zh: 本段是全文的 logical starting point，它先从动物能力切入，说明人类并非天然 unique，并为后文讨论 AI 对 intelligence 和 creativity 的冲击铺垫论证基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Meanwhile, technology has quashed(使无效), one by one, claims that cognitive tasks require a human brain. The first adding machine was invented in 1623. This past year, a computer-generated work won an art contest. I believe the moment when computers meet and surpass human intelligence is on the horizon.
zh: 本段承接前文对 human uniqueness 的质疑，并把焦点锁定 AI；它提出机器可能超越人类智能与创造力这一前提，直接引出后文“人类劳动还会如何被评价”的核心问题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: How will human intelligence and creativity be valued when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people? There will likely be a spectrum. In some domains, people still value humans doing things, even if a computer can do it better. It's been a quarter of a century since a computer beat world champion Garry Kasparov, but human chess hasn't gone away.
zh: 本段构成全文预测中的第一种情形，即 human work 仍有市场和文化价值；它使文章避免把 AI 影响写成绝对替代，也为后两段的不同情形建立 spectrum 框架。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In other fields, human skill will seem costly and redundant. Take illustration for example: most readers don't care whether the graphic accompanying a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer — they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps entertaining.
zh: 本段呈现与前段相反的第二种情形：AI 会在某些领域挤出 human workers；它具体支撑文章主旨中 AI displace many jobs 的判断，并增强论证的现实感。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: And, of course, this question isn't black or white. Many fields will be a hybrid, where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to oversee the machines.
zh: 本段补全了前两段所列的两端情况，提出更常见的 hybrid future；它进一步说明人类未必彻底消失，但可获得的位置会缩小，这与全文关于 reduced opportunities 的主旨相呼应。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: If history is any guide, it's almost certain that advances in AI will cause more jobs to vanish, that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number, and that those who own creative technology will become the new ultra-rich.
zh: 本段是全文的 concluding forecast，它把前文关于 intelligence、creativity 和 human work 的讨论落到社会经济后果：工作减少、纯人类技能者机会收缩、技术所有者积累财富，从而完整收束文章主旨。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Projects, relationships, and jobs don't always work out as planned — and it's not always clear when to give up. We've all repeatedly heard the saying that "quitters never win", but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses.
zh: 本段承担 introduction 的功能，它提出“坚持未必总对、及时止损也有价值”的核心问题，为后文分析阻碍人们 quit 的心理偏差铺路。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is. And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea.
zh: 本段把第一段的抽象观点具体化，解释了人们为什么难以放弃，并自然引出“坚持过度”这一全文需要解决的问题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit". But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.
zh: 本段进一步界定全文讨论的目标：文章不是提倡 quit，而是教读者作出辨别，因此它为后续三类 bias 的分析设定了判断标准。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into — even when abandoning it would be more beneficial. We realize that we can't get back the resources we've given, so we persevere — investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we're already halfway through it. If quitting is "not your thing", you may be especially susceptible to this bias.
zh: 本段是正文第一个原因分析，它具体揭示了阻碍明智退出的 sunk-cost bias，并为下一段的应对策略提供了直接对象。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we'll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on. To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now? Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity? Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on? For example, is it possible that you'll be throwing more good money after what you've already lost? Or that you won't have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities?
zh: 本段完成“问题—对策”的闭环：它不仅说明沉没成本为何有害，也提供可操作的 decision-making 框架，帮助读者理性止损。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome. This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health. However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action. Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.
zh: 本段引入第二种妨碍放弃的心理机制，并说明“我不是轻易放弃的人”与控制幻觉结合时，会显著增加错误加码的风险。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not. Think rigorously. While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can't force them to change or go your way.
zh: 本段为第二种 bias 提供简明工具，使读者能够把模糊的主观感觉转化为可检查的书面判断，增强是否退出的理性基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense. Expending effort and emotion on things you can't control can be both draining and disempowering.
zh: 本段强化了控制清单的实际意义，并把“是否值得继续付出”重新连接到文章的总问题：何时 persevere，何时 call it quits。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.
zh: 本段开启第三个障碍，即 rigid self-identity；它把“难以放弃”的原因从资源与控制感进一步推进到更深层的自我认同。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company. Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she'd been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, "The thing is, I'm not a quitter." This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action.
zh: 本段用具体案例验证第九段的研究结论，使抽象的 identity threat 变得可感，也为下一段提出突破固定自我的办法作准备。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior. If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics. Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here? For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, "Discernment and bravery."
zh: 本段回应 Ryan 的困境，提出通过多元自我评价来恢复决策弹性，是全文关于克服 rigid self-identity 的第一项关键策略。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself. What does the discerning part of you say? The brave part? Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices. It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.
zh: 本段把内部的 self-reflection 扩展到外部的信息搜集，说明明智 quit 不只靠意志或直觉，而需要多角度的 evidence。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. If you're considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner. Similarly, if you're looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend. In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: "How would you manage this situation?"
zh: 本段落实了上一段的 external information 建议，具体规定了应向谁求助，从而帮助读者避免只听身边利益相关者的意见。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend. Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success. External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered.
zh: 本段与第十三段共同完善外部信息策略：前者强调获得他人视角，后者强调依据客观事实，两者都在提高退出或坚持决定的准确性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn't turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical. Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break. Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience(韧性), emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset.
zh: 本段补足文章的情绪维度：理性上知道该 quit 并不意味着情感上容易接受，因此 self-compassion 是避免失败感阻碍未来行动的重要条件。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation. For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project. And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her.
zh: 本段延续 self-compassion 的主题，把宽容自己进一步转化为 growth mindset，使“放弃”从消极终止变为下一次更好决策的学习资源。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.
zh: 本段作为 conclusion 回扣全文主旨，综合肯定坚持的价值与明智退出的必要性，并以积极前景强化读者学习“何时放手”的现实意义。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
zh: 本段承担 opening function，先界定“反复给不需要的建议”这一讨论对象，并提出动机可能不单纯。它为全文主旨中的 power 和 validation 埋下伏笔，也使后文的应对策略有了心理学依据。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Under the guise(外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.
zh: 本段把第一段较宽泛的动机讨论收束为核心论点，即 unwanted advice 往往关联 power 与 control。它直接支撑文章主旨中“并非完全出于真心帮助”的判断，并为理解建议者提供同理心基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.
zh: 本段进一步补足建议者的情感画像，说明其控制行为背后可能并非只有权力欲，还有脆弱和未被妥善处理的情绪需求。这个解释为全文后面提出 compassion 和避免冲突提供了重要的心理逻辑。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.
zh: 本段是全文的 transition，从分析建议者的动机转入讨论接受者的应对方式。它否定激烈指责，为下一段解释冲突为何升级、再为第六段提出建设性边界策略作铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright(直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.
zh: 本段具体说明第4段所说 undesired result 是如何产生的，从心理威胁一路发展到更顽固的 validation-seeking 或更大冲突。它直接论证了文章主旨中“边界需要 tactfully 设置”的必要性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"
zh: 本段给出全文最核心的 practical solution，直接落实文章主旨所要求的“acknowledging without accepting”。它把前两段的心理洞察转化为可直接使用的表达，构成论证中的主要建议。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. As uncomfortable as it may be to continuously receive, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely defuse much faster.
zh: 本段补充第6段的沟通策略，强调边界是否得体还取决于接受者的情绪管理能力。它使文章主旨中的 tactfully 不再只是语言技巧，而成为 self-regulation 与 compassion 共同构成的能力。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.
zh: 本段从接受者角度重新确认边界的合法性，防止前面对建议者心理需求的理解被误读为无限忍让。它平衡了全文立场：理解对方的 underlying reasons，但也要维护自己的 emotional safety。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
zh: 本段承担 conclusion function，完整回收全文主旨：面对 unwanted advice，接受者可以而且应当设置边界，但方式要兼顾建议者的 emotional needs。它将“理解”与“拒绝”整合为减少 conflict 和 stress 的成熟处理原则。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.
zh: 本段承担引入背景的作用，先说明 interdependence 是人类社会的基础，再自然引出后文的核心概念 solidarity；它回答了“为什么需要团结”的问题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.
zh: 本段把前一段的抽象群体关系具体转化为 solidarity 的初步识别标准，为下一段的 dictionary definition 做铺垫；它完成了从社会现象到概念定义的过渡。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "... a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."
zh: 本段为全文提供概念锚点，明确 solidarity 的基本含义；后文关于 diversity、individualism 和 common good 的讨论，都会在这个 definition 的基础上进一步扩展。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.
zh: 本段扩大了概念的分析范围，提醒读者不能用简单的同质化群体理解 solidarity；它为后文介绍 communitarianism、individualism 及 genuine solidarity 的不同 facets 做准备。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism(社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy are sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.
zh: 本段介绍 solidarity 的第一个具体 facet，并揭示其潜在风险；它为全文后面寻找一种既能维持社会联系、又不压制个体的 genuine solidarity 埋下伏笔。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.
zh: 本段介绍 solidarity 的第二个 facet，并将其置于 individualism 的思想背景中；它进一步说明真正的社会联系不能建立在完全不受约束的个人选择之上。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other — in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.
zh: 本段是全文的 conclusion，既回收前文关于多种 facets 的讨论，又给出作者最终立场：solidarity 必须超越狭隘利益，成为包容、合作并维护 human dignity 的社会纽带。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: It's best to think of an accent as a distinct, systematic and rule-governed way of speaking. Accent is not a synonym for dialect, but it's related. Dialect is an umbrella term for the way a community pronounces words, creates words, and orders words; accent refers to that first part only.
zh: 本段承担全文的 conceptual foundation 作用，先澄清 accent 的准确含义，避免读者把它与 dialect 混淆；这一铺垫也为后文讨论所谓 standard accent 是否存在提供了清晰的讨论对象。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Many laymen presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is inherently the best form of speech, but linguists(语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a reality. In other words, no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books.
zh: 本段是全文的 thesis paragraph，直接挑战“存在唯一标准口音”的传统观念；它把文章从概念定义推进到核心论点，即标准口音并非客观现实，而是一种被想象和建构出来的规范。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: One reason linguists agree there is no one true standard is that, through the years, there have been multiple supposed standards, depending on time and place. The standard for English in British newsreels(新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. In fact, there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon — and broadcast outlets across the spectrum have never consistently held to those standards anyway.
zh: 本段为上一段“标准口音只是理想模型”的观点补充了 historical and regional evidence；它说明标准不仅是理想化的，而且即使在看似正式的媒体语言中，也始终处于变化和不一致之中。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Even so, this idea of a standard accent is influential and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that deviate from the current standard are less appropriate, or even inappropriate. Scholars have found that southern US accent features are more accepted in domains such as government, law and service-oriented workplaces, but less accepted in the technology sector. The acceptability of nonstandard accents may correlate with differences in class and culture, with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace.
zh: 本段完成全文的现实落点：即便 standard accent 是 imagined construct，它仍会影响教育和就业中的评价与机会；因此文章最终揭示，口音标准问题不仅关乎 language，也关乎 class、culture 和社会权力。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Timed traffic lights are set according to schedules that are supposed to coordinate with peak traffic hours. Cities need to monitor and update signal light time schedules at least every two years to keep these systems effective. In Los Angeles, California, an ambitious project to go a step further and synchronize(使同步) every red light in Los Angeles cost over 400 million dollars. Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it. If implemented nationwide, synchronization could shave 10% off traffic congestion(堵塞) and 20% off air pollution. Congestion costs time, money, and lives. Big data can help improve how millions of people safely share the road. However, none of this would be possible without the traffic light!
zh: 该段作为全文的引入，用现代场景让读者认识到 traffic light 的重要性，为后面 history 和 meaning 的展开奠定了现实 relevance。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The first traffic light was invented in London in the 1860's, but it was hardly recognizable — or effective. It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868. The railroads used red gas lights at night to signal stops and green gas lights during the daytime. Knight installed a similar gas light, semaphore(臂板信号) system near London's Westminster Bridge in December of 1868.
zh: 该段正式开启文章的历史叙事，从 London 1868 出发，正好呼应文章主旨中的 "traces the evolution from 1860s origin in London"。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The life of the first traffic light signal was short-lived. A gas leak caused one of the signal lights to explode on its police officer operator within a month of being installed.
zh: 这个短段落承担叙事中的转折功能，from first invention to failure，为后文说明美国和后期发展的必要提供了动力。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Automating traffic signals stalled after the London incident. Forty years passed before cars crowding city streets urged the development of traffic lights in the United States. London would not see another traffic light until 1929.
zh: 这段是 transition 段落，连接早期 London 与未来的 US history，同时说明汽车交通是推动交通灯复兴的主要因素。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The United States is a car culture like no other country. Unlike most European cities that started urban planning when horses were high-tech, many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars.
zh: 该段提供社会文化背景，让读者理解 why traffic light development found fertile ground in the US，与文章主旨中的 "automobile-centric cities" 精准呼应。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems. The first traffic signals were semaphores. Semaphores are towers with moving arms signaling for traffic to stop or go. They could be manual or automatic. There was no consistent design. Various models were invented and put into place in cities as the need arose.
zh: 该段落从美国城市需求出发，介绍 semaphore 这种早期信号设备，并指出其多样而无序的特征，为后面 electric signals and standardization 的叙述做铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In 1912, Lester Wire was a police officer exhausted by traffic at Main Street and 200 South. He developed a manually switched stop light. The four-sided box, raised on a ten-foot pole, looked like a birdhouse and was operated manually by an officer. The officer would flip a switch to change between the dipped red and green lights.
zh: 该段具体展示 1912 年美国的一个手动信号灯，说明 early electric traffic lights 仍依赖人力，为后面 automatization 的进步作 contrast。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Like the 1910 semaphore, the first electric signal used words. However, the words were no longer written on arms that raised and fell. The words "stop" or "move" were on lights. The posts lit up on each of four corner-posts around an intersection(十字路口). It was not automated, though. A booth with an operator was required to flip the switches.
zh: 该段展示从 semaphore 到 electric light 的过渡，并强调 still manual，使读者理解为什么需要下一阶段 automation。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The system allowed police officers to move from the middle of the street to a corner. From that vantage(有利地位), an officer could oversee the crowd. If an emergency vehicle came, the officer could flip a switch and clear the intersection by triggering all red lights. The emergency vehicle could now pass effortlessly. Finally, in San Francisco the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917.
zh: 这段完成了从 manual to automatic 的关键过渡，并把地点转移到美国旧金山，突出美国在交通灯技术上的快速进步。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In 1920, the first three-color light system was introduced in Detroit — also known as Motor City, USA. The evolution of traffic light signals could not have a more appropriate context than Motor City. Ford Motor Company was founded in Detroit in 1903 (and other motor companies followed). Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production.
zh: 该段提出三色系统的诞生，并把它放在汽车工业的背景下，为接下来解释 yellow light 的必要性提供历史因果。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Stop and go were insufficient for the new volumes of cars zooming through intersections. Streets were full of new numbers of cars in addition to delivery wagons, bustling crowds, bicycles, horse-drawn carriages, and street cars. The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights.
zh: 该段说明了三色系统中黄色灯的功能价值，把 technical evolution 与 safety improvement 连接起来，符合文章主旨中的 “improve safety”。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Stop lights were incredibly important in chaotic city streets. Crosswalks weren't even introduced until 1951. The first pedestrian fatality in the United States was in 1899.
zh: 该段补充了交通灯在行人安全上的意义，与文章主旨中 “improve safety” 直接对应，也使交通灯的重要性更加立体。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The development of the modern traffic light may have started in London, but it grew up in the United States. In Cleveland, an African-American inventor named Garrett Morgan came up with an affordable, patented traffic signal. The yellow light made intersections safer than the old stop and go system. The new design was inexpensive enough that it allowed the installation of a lot more lights.
zh: 该段引入 Garrett Morgan 的重要贡献，同时解释经济因素如何推动交通灯的 spread，与文章历史线中的 evolution 和 adoption 相契合。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Morgan sold the patent to General Electric — and the spread of the traffic light was green lighted. Green means go. It is that simple, but it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light. Yellow means slow down and prepare to stop. It does not mean full-throttle(全速) ahead. While you may get away with gunning it into the intersection, running a yellow can lead to tickets and dangerous accidents. Red lights are a clear and consistent warning to stop. Even where right turns are allowed on red lights, you must come to a complete stop before turning right. You must also yield to any through traffic, which has the right of way. In most states and cities, you can take a right on red unless otherwise indicated. New York City does not allow a right on red.
zh: 该段在历史叙述结束后转向 “meaning” 主题，解释三种基本颜色，并补充驾驶细则，使文章同时具备历史与实用说明两个维度。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Red arrows mean you cannot turn right on a red in most states. The green arrow, in these cases, is the only time you can make the turn. However, you can take a right on a red arrow after a full stop in the states of Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Oregon, South Carolina, Utah, Washington State and Wyoming.
zh: 该段将信号灯含义扩展到箭头形态和不同州的法律差异，体现交通灯规则的 fine-grained 和 local variation，是 “meaning” part 的重要细化。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Flashing Red is the same as a stop sign, generally used at four-way intersections where there is minimal traffic. When arriving at a flashing red light, make a full and complete stop. Flashing Red Arrows similarly mean to stop and then proceed to take the turn. Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution, like outside of a fire station. There are no all-direction flashing yellow lights, since it is prohibited in the United States. If you have a flashing yellow light, you are to yield to oncoming traffic.
zh: 这部分继续丰富 “meaning” 主题，说明闪烁形态的信号灯在特殊路口的使用规则，让读者了解除了 solid lights 外的常见变体。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Flashing Yellow Arrows are part of a four-signal traffic light. These are used in some states after a protected green turn signal, or arrow, but before a steady yellow arrow. When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic. Steady Yellow Arrows maintain the normal yellow light caution in three-light signals, meaning to stop or prepare to stop. In a four-signal system that has a flashing yellow arrow, the steady yellow arrow is a signal that the yield period is ending. The red arrow is about to start. Vehicles should stop if safely possible. Traffic tickets are possible for running a steady yellow arrow.
zh: 该段是 “meaning” 部分最细致的示例，展示了现代四信号系统如何通过不同箭头状态提供更安全、更灵活的转弯控制。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations. Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution). Yellow means caution and yield. Red means danger and stop. Always drive defensively and obey traffic signals.
zh: 该段收束全文，将前文复杂的信号灯规则归结为简单、一致的颜色含义，并呼吁安全驾驶，与文章主旨中的 “managing traffic and improving safety” 形成圆满回响。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The other day I had to log into a service I hadn't used before. Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn't a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine.
zh: 本段是全文的 narrative hook，它用人人熟悉的数字场景降低阅读门槛；同时，“prove”与“robot”的对照为文章主旨中的人机关系异化提供了第一个具体入口。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid. My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. I did so, a bit irritated. Then I was presented with another image and another grid — also with a request to identify road signs. Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.
zh: 本段把第一段抽象的 Captcha 变成可观察的 labor process；作者的无奈顺从预先强化了文章主旨中的 subtle conditioning，即人们在便利服务面前不知不觉接受系统安排。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: And then I realised what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine-learning software that guides self-driving cars. So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labor to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles.
zh: 这是全文论证的关键 evidence paragraph，它将个人烦恼提升为商业与技术问题；它直接支撑文章主旨，即数字技术把人当作实现其商业 ends 的手段，而非服务人类利益的工具。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Neat, eh? But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!
zh: 本段由具体的 unpaid labor 进一步深化到象征层面：人机关系不只是利益分配不公，更出现了权力与判断权的 reversal；这强化了全文对技术支配人的忧虑。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been. The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us? Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by "smart" tech, trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves?
zh: 本段把前文的个案提升为社会心理诊断，补足文章主旨中“subtly conditioned”与“under-discussed”两层含义；它说明问题之所以危险，恰恰在于多数人没有意识到自己正在适应它。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars — Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher — argue that the answer to that question is "yes".
zh: 本段承担承上启下作用：它承接第五段的设问并给出肯定回答，也为末段“And they're right”的作者明确表态提供了逻辑台阶，使全文批评不显得只是个人抱怨。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: And they're right. There's nothing technophobic(技术恐惧的) about that. We shape our tools and then our tools shape us. Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends. But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours. In the process, they reduce us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills(踏车) designed by people who do not have our interests at heart. So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.
zh: 本段完成全文的 conclusion：它从 Captcha 例子归纳出技术伦理上的根本矛盾，即人被系统化地工具化；同时以悲观反问收束，呼应“温水青蛙”隐喻，突出文章对这种趋势长期且未被充分讨论的深层警告。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits — it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness.
zh: 本段作为全文的 introduction，先建立 mindfulness 值得讨论的健康价值，为后文解释其原理、社会意义及人际价值提供了论述起点。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it. This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.
zh: 本段承接首段的健康效果，进一步回答正念 why it works：它通过非反应性的观察，防止情绪和思维不断扩大。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad. It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.
zh: 本段完成从原理到效果的推导，并为全文后面强调 fully present 埋下伏笔，使正念由个人情绪管理自然过渡到现实生活中的注意力问题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention. The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell. This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment.
zh: 本段是全文的重要转折，从个人内部的正念机制转向社会外部的注意力危机，并为下一段论证 mindfulness 如何 resist this economy 铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment. The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen. But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love.
zh: 本段直接呼应文章主旨中 resist the attention economy 的部分，说明正念不仅有健康作用，也是一种对抗现代分心生活的实践工具。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.
zh: 本段是全文第二次关键转向，它把正念的价值从 self 扩展到 others，并引出后文关于倾听、同情和关系建设的具体论述。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners. However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it's possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment.
zh: 本段把抽象的“为他人练习正念”具体化为 listening 的能力，同时为下一段列举正念倾听的实际做法做好逻辑准备。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences. To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions. It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.
zh: 本段是全文论证的具体落地部分，它将正念从理念转化为可操作的人际行为，并完整呈现文章主旨中的 mindful listening。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one.
zh: 本段收束全文，将健康、抗干扰和人际倾听三条论线凝聚为最终主张：在 attention economy 主导的时代，专注倾听本身就是最珍贵的 gift。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Two proposals are before the state legislature that look to put some limits on ever-increasing rent prices, which some lawmakers say are contributing to rising homelessness rates.
zh: 本段承担 lead paragraph 的功能，用 proposals、rent prices 和 homelessness 快速搭建报道框架；它为下文的政策细则、支持证据及反对声音提供了共同的讨论中心。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The proposals impose caps on rent increases, preventing landlords in the state from raising rent more than the rate of inflation in most cases. There are exceptions for buildings less than 10 years old, public housing, improvements beyond maintenance, and a hardship exemption.
zh: 本段把首段较抽象的 rent limits 落实为可执行的机制，并用 exceptions 预先回应政策可能过于僵化的疑问；它让读者理解争议的具体对象，而不只是笼统的“租金管制”。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In a 2020 study, researchers at the U.S. Government Accountability Office estimated that every $100 in rent increase is correlated to a 9% rise in homelessness. Rent increases have an even more detrimental effect on some demographic groups, such as racial minorities.
zh: 本段为支持 rent-control proposals 的一方补充实证依据，使首段中“租金导致 homelessness”的主张更可信；对 racial minorities 的补充还赋予该政策社会公平层面的意义。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Representative Alex Ramel explained why he thought that this kind of legislation was so important, telling the story of a constituent struggling to live in the community.
zh: 本段是从宏观 research 转向微观 human story 的过渡，它让支持立法的论证由统计数据延伸到具体居民的生活处境，并自然衔接下一段的直接引语。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Ramel pointed out the devastating effect of double-digit rent increases, saying that he made the decision to introduce the legislation while talking to a young man in Bellingham. "He's a recent graduate from Western Washington University and just got a new job," Ramel said. "He was leaving our community because his landlord notified him that his rent was going to go up by $600 a month."
zh: 本段把 rent increase 与 homelessness 风险之间的宏观关联具象化为一个可感知的 displacement case；它强化了 Ramel 的支持理由，也展示该政策意在保护的对象和后果。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The Rental Housing Association of Washington opposes the legislation. The association asserts that the policy won't actually solve the problem of rental prices. Instead, it will punish small landlords and allow wealthy renters easy access to cheap housing.
zh: 本段引入 landlord groups 的正式反对意见，使报道呈现 balanced coverage；它直接对应文章主旨中的反方论点，并为最后一段更强烈的批评性引语作铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: "The rent control policy has failed everywhere it has been enacted in this county. It has not fixed one housing problem anywhere. It also does not distinguish between rich and poor when determining who gets the benefits of rent control," said Chester Baldwin with the Rental Housing Coalition.
zh: 本段以反对方的直接 quote 收束报道，完整呈现其对 effectiveness 与 equity 的两重质疑；它与前文支持者的研究数据和个人案例形成鲜明对照，落实全文“政策争议”的主线。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: For those "citizens of the world", the office can be anything from a beach hut in Brisbane to a Starbucks in Seattle, thanks to the growing prevalence of remote-based work. But roaming the globe from café to café is not without its challenges.
zh: 本段引入 remote work 和 global mobility 两个关键词，帮助读者快速进入 digital nomad 的主题。它还提前埋下 challenges 这一线索，使全文不会被理解成单纯赞美自由旅行的文章。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: When the average traveller lands in a city like Bangkok, Berlin, or Buenos Aires, their first step might be to drop their bags at their hotel and to log on to TripAdvisor to find out the hours of a popular tourist attraction or the best rooftop bar for happy hour.
zh: 本段看似只是生活化的 travel scene，实际上承担了 contrast setup 的功能。它先让读者理解普通游客如何使用城市，再为数字游民与城市之间的 different relationship 做准备。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But people like Pieter Levels are not your average traveller. A Dutch website developer, Levels has been living and working nomadically(像游牧民那样) in places like Singapore, Hong Kong, Tokyo and Manila for two years. With just a carry-on backpack, he chooses his location at will, based on a variety of factors—Wi-Fi speed, average temperature, exotic food and cost of living—that have little bearing on the work he actually does.
zh: 本段通过 Levels 这个 individual example 展示数字游民的具体形态。它把文章从普通游客的 background transition 到数字游民的 lifestyle description，并为下一段的 online infrastructure 埋下需求基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Somewhere in his nomadic journey, Levels noticed that there was a growing need to create an online infrastructure for people like himself. That's when he created #nomads, a membership-based chat system which runs on the team communication platform known as Slack. The channel allows users to ask people in their current city the types of practical questions that a tourist would unlikely need to ask.
zh: 本段把个人体验提升为 community response，说明数字游民已经形成一定的 shared needs。它进一步证明 technology 不只是工作工具，也是这种 borderless lifestyle 得以维系的重要 infrastructure。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Members of the geographically dispersed subculture that Levels is a part of call themselves "digital nomads". They are borderless, mostly self-employed remote workers who interact with cities in a way that's entirely different from a tourist, but still doesn't quite reach the status of resident. A relatively new phenomenon, there are no hard statistics on the prevalence of digital nomads or location independent workers. But thanks to the growing prevalence of freelance(自由职业的) livelihoods, a global sharing economy and numerous digital tools, the number of people who are able to live this life is growing quickly. And in a rapidly urbanising world, where a major city in Asia increasingly offers the same comforts as one in Europe, many people are reaching the realisation they don't need to stay in one place.
zh: 本段是全文的 conceptual core，因为它正式解释 digital nomad 是谁以及为何增长。它把前文的个案提升为社会现象，并为后文讨论身份差异、生活挑战和 privilege 提供总体框架。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: So how does a nomad differ from a tourist or resident? In many ways, Levels says, you can think of a digital nomad like a "short-term independent expat(移居国外的人)". Unlike a resident expat, they don't work for a large multinational company in an air conditioned office building and they generally enter a country on a tourist visa, simply renewing or moving on when it expires. But unlike a tourist, they don't arrive in a foreign city without any responsibilities. Travel isn't necessarily required for them to do their jobs, but neither is staying in one place.
zh: 本段为 digital nomad 提供清晰的 category boundary，帮助读者避免把他们误认为 tourists 或 company expatriates。它深化了文章主旨中的 distinctive lifestyle，尤其强调 mobility 并不等于 complete freedom。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Janet Brent is an independent ebook designer. She says many people she knows assume she travels for work, but in reality her international destinations are largely up to her, and driven by cost. "Contrary to what some people might think, I don't get paid to travel—I simply choose the lifestyle. Rather than rent in one given city, I choose to travel and do short-term, temporary stays around the world, and my travel decisions are literally based on what makes the most sense financially for me," Brent said. "It's completely different from vacationing—you really sink into the city life and get your feet wet in the communities."
zh: 本段通过 Brent 的 first-person testimony 丰富了数字游民的生活图景。它说明 nomadic life 不是被公司安排的 travel assignment，而是个人主动选择的、具有经济考量和文化参与的 lifestyle。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Bryce Adams is another such nomad. He works as a developer for a South African company WooThemes, which has a workforce that's more than 80% remote-based. Though Adams frequently posts pictures on Instagram of his enviable cooking adventures from Seoul to Bangkok, he says nomad life in foreign cities has its downsides, including finding adequate Wi-Fi for the bandwidth-hungry work his livelihood depends on. Contrary to the perception that he works under a mango tree in a tropical haven, Adams says the reality of this life means that he often ends up staying in more western style places in globalised cities—ones that are sure to have air conditioning and a decent connection—rather than exotic beachfront cafés.
zh: 本段把文章主旨中的 practical challenges 具体化为 Wi-Fi 和办公环境问题。它也削弱了“数字游民每天在海滩工作”的 romantic stereotype，使读者看到 freedom 背后的 technical dependence。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: "A fellow nomad posted quite a funny but honest message on Twitter a few days ago that stuck with me: 'It's funny that digital nomads spend 16 hours to fly to the other side of the world to sit in Starbucks,' and it's completely true," Adams said. "When you're a digital nomad, you don't actually have as much freedom as most people think you do. We have deadlines, we all have people relying on us and a mouth (or two) that needs to be fed. It's nice to be able to work anywhere in the world but it's not without its challenges."
zh: 本段继续展开 digital nomads 的 challenges，并具体说明他们并非没有约束的自由旅行者。它强化了全文的 balanced perspective：地点自由存在，但 professional responsibility 同样真实。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But these challenges can often provide an opportunity for nomads to see a side of a city they may not have if they were staying in a luxury hotel for a long weekend. However inconvenient, a trip to a local doctor, immigration office or laundry—or a conflict with a local Airbnb host (the accommodation style of choice for most nomads)—can be far more culturally instructive than a trip to the national museum. And because nomads often have to stay where the strongest internet connection is, they tend to spend more time in developing cities compared to the average tourist, who often flees to more touristy destinations soon after landing at the airport.
zh: 本段没有继续单纯罗列困难，而是说明 challenges 也能带来 deeper cultural experiences。它为文章主旨增加了 cultural dimension，并解释了数字游民为何可能比普通游客更了解 developing cities。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The nomad life is, by all accounts, one built out of privilege. You not only need a relatively powerful passport that makes tourist visas easy to attain, but also a knowledge economy job and access to the technology and devices that make remote working possible. But nomads like Adams say that while they are aware of this privilege, they believe living this way elevates what they're able to offer, by giving them a broader perspective on what they're building, writing, or designing and expanding their world view.
zh: 本段为文章加入 social critique，提醒读者数字游民现象背后存在 passport、job 和 technology inequalities。与此同时，它承认 travel 能带来 perspective gains，使全文对该 lifestyle 的评价更加完整和客观。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: "Being able to travel and get around makes it easy to stay inspired," he added. "I truly believe that it makes me a more sensible human being, as I tend to see and appreciate the creative solutions people come up with in other parts of the world, even though many tend to have far more constraints than we have at home."
zh: 本段具体补充了 nomadic travel 的 intellectual value，使“拓展视野”不再是抽象口号。它说明全球经历能够培养 inspiration、appreciation 和 empathy，从而支撑全文对数字游民积极作用的论述。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: So when you're constantly on the road and don't own any property or have a fixed address, which city do you call home? It's no surprise that many nomads are dual citizens or "third culture kids," who have grown up with a notion of identity that's not tied to nationalism or staying in one place. Levels says that the nomad life has not only changed his notions of citizenship, but the people he chooses to spend time with as well. "Saying you're a 'citizen of the world' is a super cliché, right? But it's becoming quite true," Levels said. "This global awareness has been the reason I started Nomad List and it's affected who my friends are. It's normal to have dinner now and sit with a Korean girl, a British-Singaporean guy, a Mexican girl and a Nigerian guy. As much as that sounds like a politically correct TV advertisement, it's great that that's the time we're in now."
zh: 本段完成了全文的 thematic elevation：文章不再只讨论在哪里工作，而是讨论这种生活如何改变 home、citizenship 和 community。它最终回应文章主旨中的 expanded perspectives，并把数字游民现象提升为对全球化身份的观察。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: About a decade ago, the G-20, a forum of the world's biggest economies, agreed to crack down on multinational corporations' abusive use of tax havens. This resulted in a plan that aimed to curb practices that shielded a large chunk of corporate profits from tax authorities.
zh: 本段承担 introduction 的任务，先建立“国际社会已经出手”的基线。正因为已有 coordinated effort，后文的 But 才能突出治理结果与初衷之间的 sharp contrast，并支撑全文要求更有效改革的论证。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But, instead of reining in the use of tax havens—countries such as the Bahamas and Cayman Islands with very low or no effective tax rates—the problem has only gotten worse.
zh: 本段是全文的 problem statement，它把第一段的改革承诺转化为现实失败。这个反差推动作者必须继续提供 evidence，解释利润转移究竟有多严重，以及应采取何种 solution。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In a new study, we measured the excessive profits reported in tax havens that cannot be explained by ordinary economic activity such as employees, factories and research in that country. Our findings show a striking pattern of artificial shifting of paper profits to tax havens by corporations, which has been relentless since the 1980s.
zh: 本段为文章的核心判断提供 empirical evidence，即企业利润并非自然流向避税天堂，而是被 artificially shifted。它因此把第二段的笼统“恶化”转化为可论证的事实基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: We found that the world's biggest multinational businesses shifted 37% of the profits—$969 billion—they earned in other countries to tax havens in 2019. The figure was less than 2% in the 1970s. The main reasons for the large increase were the growth of the tax avoidance industry in the 1980s and U.S. policies that made it easier to shift profits from high-tax countries to tax havens.
zh: 本段把问题的严重性具体化，并首次解释其增长机制。大量利润被 shifted 的事实直接支撑文章主旨中的 increasingly shift profits，同时 causes 指向后文应消除税率差异这一政策论点。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: We estimate that the amount of corporate taxes lost as a result reached 10% of total corporate revenue in 2019, up from less than 0.1% in the 1970s. In 2019, the total government tax loss globally was $250 billion. U.S. multinational corporations alone accounted for about half of that, followed by the U.K. and Germany.
zh: 本段回答了“为什么必须解决”这一关键问题，即 profit shifting 损害政府筹资能力。它直接呼应文章主旨中的 depriving governments of substantial tax revenue，并增强改革建议的 urgency。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: How do policymakers fix this? So far, the world as a whole has been trying to solve this problem by cutting or scrapping corporate taxes in a very gradual way. In the past 40 years, the global effective corporate tax rate has fallen from 23% to 17%. At the same time, governments have relied more heavily on consumption taxes.
zh: 本段展示现行政策背景，即国家并未统一抬高约束，而是在 corporate tax competition 中继续降低税率。这为下一段提出 global minimum tax 提供必要的对照，也暗示现行 approach 未触及根本原因。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But the root cause of profit-shifting is the incentives involved, such as generous or lenient corporate tax rates in other countries. If countries could agree on a global minimum corporate tax rate of, say, 20%, the problem of profit-shifting would largely disappear, as tax havens would simply cease to exist.
zh: 本段是全文的 central argument，它从税率激励这一根因推导出最低税率这一解法。它最直接地落实文章主旨中 coordinated global tax reform 和 meaningful minimum corporate tax rate 的核心主张。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: This type of mechanism is exactly what more than 130 countries signed onto in 2021, with implementation of a 15% minimum tax set to begin soon in the EU, U.K., Japan, Indonesia and many other countries. The U.S. has notably not been able to pass this legislation.
zh: 本段用现实行动证明最低税改革具有 feasibility，并补充其执行缺口。它使文章的建议不止停留在 theory，同时提示美国这一主要经济体的缺席会影响全球改革的完整性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Our research suggests implementing this type of tax reform is necessary in reversing the shift of ever-greater amounts of corporate profits to tax havens—instead of being taxed by the governments where they operate and create value.
zh: 本段完成 conclusion，将前文的失败现状、研究证据、税收损失、根因和改革实践收束为最终立场。它完整回扣全文主旨：只有协调的 tax reform，才能阻止利润流向避税天堂并恢复价值创造地的征税权。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Children's use of social media is a problem. That doesn't mean it should be stopped. While younger children should not be on platforms where 13 is the minimum age, it is neither practical nor desirable to imagine a world in which teenagers are prevented from accessing the platforms and messaging systems that the adults around them use to organise their lives.
zh: 本段为全文建立了基本 framework：作者既不主张 unrestricted access，也不主张 total prohibition。这个 moderate starting point 为后文讨论 depression、regulation 和 company accountability 提供了逻辑前提，使全文呈现出 balanced argument 的特点。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But the pleasure and stimulation that people of all ages find on their screens and smartphones must not blind us to the harm that spending time in this way can cause. The finding that the alarmingly high rate of depression in British teenage girls is closely correlated to time spent on social media is extremely concerning. Research found that two in five girls are on social media for at least three hours a day—with half as many boys engaged to the same extent. More than a third of depressed girls have experienced online harassment. About half of affected girls suffered disrupted sleep, compared with 20% of depressed boys.
zh: 本段为文章主旨提供了 empirical support，解释了为什么 teenagers' social media use 不能被视为 harmless。它特别凸显 teenage girls 的 vulnerability，并列出 depression、online harassment 和 sleep disruption 等相关问题，为后文要求 clearer guidance、stronger regulation 和 greater accountability 奠定了事实基础。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Although the research does not prove that social media causes depression, the importance of the finding that there is a connection should not be underestimated. Schools have done important work in communicating key messages about the risks of online abuse. But when it comes to broader questions about "screen time", many professionals as well as parents are confused and uncertain.
zh: 本段在逻辑上承担 qualification 的作用，避免全文滑向 oversimplification。它既维护了文章的 scientific caution，又说明现有 evidence 足以支持进一步关注和制定 guidance，从而自然过渡到下一段的 government initiatives 与 regulation。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The health secretary, Matt Hancock, wants official guidelines on time and age limits. This idea has the virtue of simplicity, though some experts question its effects and call for a greater degree of differentiation, arguing that time online by itself is not a bad thing and it all depends on what you are doing. Also due this year is information commissioner Elizabeth Denham's Age Appropriate Design Code, covering the use of children's personal data. Both initiatives are welcome. But the government is playing catch-up. Statutory regulation of the digital media giants is long overdue. The failure to protect children from data harvesting and targeted advertising thus far is as shocking as the lack of concern shown by the companies themselves with regard to children's psychological health.
zh: 本段把前文提出的 risk 和 uncertainty 转化为 policy demands，直接回应文章主旨中的 clearer guidance 和 stronger regulation。与此同时，它把责任主体从 individual users 扩展到 government 与 technology companies，强化了全文关于 institutional accountability 的论证。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Of course, social media companies are not the source of all our ills, and can offer a too-easy target for politicians keen to divert attention from inadequately resourced schools and health services. There are other reasons for the rising incidence of depression in young people, with increasing pressure to succeed in education and in life more broadly—to be famous, beautiful, rich—often cited as a source of unhappiness or anxiety which can, if aggravated by other factors and not managed, tip into ill health. Safeguarding means more than the avoidance of physical threat.
zh: 本段为全文提供 necessary balance 和 final qualification，防止读者把文章理解成单纯 blame technology。它最终重申文章主旨的完整边界：social media risks require guidance、regulation 和 company accountability，但解决 youth mental-health problems 还需要面对更广泛的 social causes。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Most financial crises have plenty in common: they tend to start in the banking sector and involve excessive borrowing, together with an asset bubble. The global crisis of 2008 was no different, with the asset bubble focused on US real estate. But my research suggests this crisis had another underlying cause—that some people in the banking sector were playing or "gaming" the system for their own financial gain.
zh: 本段承担 introduction 的任务：先承认 2008 crisis 的 conventional causes，再引出 bankers gaming the system 这一全文 explanatory thread。它把文章从“危机有什么表面特征”推进到“金融从业者如何通过制度获利”，为后文分析 complexity、bias、risk 和 bailout expectation 铺路。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The game being played had several important features. The first was the deliberate complexity of the financial products at its core. Then there are the behavioural biases that permeate decision-making at all levels of the banking industry. Banking often attracts people with certain personality traits, including those who are overconfident and take excessive risks.
zh: 本段承担 mechanism mapping 的作用，把第一段提出的 gaming 概念拆成 product-level complexity 和 human-level bias。它还通过 overconfidence 与 excessive risk-taking 建立与第三、第四段的 logical bridge，使全文从“有这种行为”推进到“这种行为由哪些因素促成”。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Such people tend to like complexity for its own sake, but they often do not fully understand the implications of that complexity for the stability of the financial system as a whole. Often they do not care—they are primarily interested in gaming the system to maximise their bonuses.
zh: 本段把第二段的 personality traits 转译成具体 behavior 和 incentive：complexity 被偏好，systemic stability 被忽视，bonuses 成为主要目标。这样，文章主旨中的 personal gain 获得了具体说明，也解释了 banking game 为什么会伤害 the financial system as a whole。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The next element is risk. There are parts of the banking sector that will always be prone to risk, but many bankers have come to feel immune to its potential impact, because they presume that, however recklessly banks behave, governments will always be there to bail them out.
zh: 本段将第三段的个人逐利连接到 risk-taking mechanism，说明 reckless behavior 为什么能够持续。government bailouts 形成 implicit safety net，使 private gain 与 public loss 相分离，从而直接支撑文章关于 excessive risk-taking 的主旨。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Gaming in the banking sector seems virtually impossible to eliminate. The only effective measure to end it would be to make bankers personally liable for losses, but no government has ever passed such a law, and no single government could do so on its own, since this would immediately cause their entire national banking sector to move wholesale to another jurisdiction.
zh: 本段完成全文的 conclusion：提出 personal liability 作为唯一有效 remedy，又说明 single-government action 会受到 jurisdictional competition 的限制。这样文章从 causes（complexity、bias、risk、bailouts）推进到 reform failure，最终解释了 why gaming persists，并照应总主旨。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Five hundred years ago, forests covered much of the Iberian peninsula. But that soon changed. Centuries of wars and invasions, agricultural expansion and woodcutting for firewood and shipping wiped out most of the woods and transformed places like Matamorisca, a small village in northern Spain, into degraded landscapes.
zh: 本段交代了森林退化的 origin 和 historical causes，说明后文的 restoration efforts 是在回应长期形成的生态问题。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: The region's dry climate and depleted soils would be a recipe for disaster in your average program to replant trees, but for the Amsterdam-based Land Life Company it's an ideal place. "We typically operate where nature does not come back by itself," says Jurrian Ruys, its CEO. "We go where there are rougher conditions in terms of weather, with rough or very hot summers." In Matamorisca, they intervened in 17 barren hectares owned by the regional government and peppered them with their signature device: a biodegradable(可生物降解的) cardboard container they call the cocoon which can hold 25 litres of water underground to aid a seedling's first year. Around 16,000 trees, including oaks, ashes, walnuts, rowans, and whitebeams, were planted in May 2018, and the company reports that 96% of them survived that year's burning hot summer without extra irrigation, a critical milestone for a young tree.
zh: 本段提供了全文第一个 concrete solution，证明 reforestation 不只是理念，也可以借助技术在极端环境中实际推进。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: "Does nature return by itself?" asks Arnout Asjes, Land Life Company's chief technology officer, who oversees a mix of drone(无人机) and satellite imagery, big data analysis, soil enhancement, QR(二维码) tagging and site-specific tree configuration designs. "Probably, but it can take decades or hundreds of years, so we are speeding things up."
zh: 本段解释了 Land Life Company 为什么需要介入自然过程，进一步强化 technology 在全文恢复模式中的功能。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: His company belongs to a global movement of organisations trying to save degraded or deforested areas, ranging from fertile tropical lowlands to dry hills in temperate(温带的) regions. Spurred by global biodiversity loss and climate change, these groups are pushing the boundary of how to revive forest cover. "It's not a theoretical proposition," says Walter Vergara, a forest and climate specialist at the World Resources Institute(WRI). "It requires the right incentives, the right stakeholders, the right analysis and sufficient capital, but it can happen."
zh: 本段把 Matamorisca 的 local experiment 放入全球森林修复背景中，使文章从个案报道发展为对 global efforts 的整体介绍。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: How these factors come together for a particular project—and whether saving destroyed woods is even possible—depends on what kind of ecosystem you have in mind. Secondary forests in the Amazon are different from Texas pines recovering after wildfires or the Arctic timber woods that cover much of Sweden. Each provides different reasons for reforestation programs and each has particular needs. In the dry conditions around Matamorisca and similar areas in Spain, Land Life Company worries about rapid desertification(沙漠化). As its focus is on restoring an ecosystem, it works with organisations that don't expect their money back.
zh: 本段建立了全文的重要判断标准：reforestation 是否可行以及如何实施，取决于当地 ecosystem 和项目的 funding purpose。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: With around 600 hectares replanted around the world since 2015 and another 1,100 planned for this year, the company's drive fits into the Bonn Challenge, a global effort to restore 150 million hectares of the world's deforested and degraded land by 2020. That's an area roughly the size of Iran or Mongolia. By 2030, the goal is to reach 350 million hectares—20% more land than India. These targets include both the rehabilitation of forested areas that have lost density or look a bit weak (a process known as 'restoration' in forestry jargon) and the recovery of forest cover in areas where it was completely cleared (what's known as 'reforestation').
zh: 本段把前文的 individual project 与国际性 target 对接，说明生态修复已经成为具有明确数量目标的 global agenda。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: That global target is broken into smaller pieces and takes shape in Latin America as the 20x20 Initiative, an effort to contribute 20 million hectares to the overall goal by initiating small to medium projects with the political backing of governments. Unlike Land Life Company, this region-wide project makes the economic and business case for reforestation, even though they are after biodiversity conservation. "You need to bring in private sector money," says WRI's Vergara, who leads the initiative, "and that capital needs to see a return on their investment." A study he led predicts Latin America would see an estimated net present value of about $23bn over a 50-year period if it reaches its goal.
zh: 本段引入 reforestation 的 investment dimension，为后文介绍 timber、carbon credits 和 ecotourism 等收入来源做好铺垫。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Money can come from timber sales in sustainably managed forests or from harvesting 'non-wood products' like nuts, oils and fruits from the trees. You can take note of how much carbon dioxide your forest is capturing and sell carbon credits to companies keen to offset their emissions. Or you can even grow the forest hoping that biodiversity will attract ecotourists who'd pay for lodging, birdwatching tours and meals.
zh: 本段将上一段的 financial return 具体化，展示环境修复可以通过多元化 business models 获得经济支持。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Still, these backers are not your high-street bank. Money for the 20x20 Initiative comes mostly from financial organisations with triple goal—a modest return on their investment, environmental benefits and social gains—known as impact investors. Take the German fund 12Tree for instance, one of the 20x20 partners. It put $9.5 million into Cuango, a 1,455-hectare property on the Caribbean coast of Panama that combines a commercial cocoa tree plantation with timber extraction from a sustainably managed secondary forest. With their money, they reforested a former cattle ranch, provided high-quality jobs for the surrounding communities and made a return on their investment.
zh: 本段通过具体投资案例说明 private capital 并不必然与生态保护冲突，关键在于设计兼顾回报和公共利益的项目。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Even on land cleared decades ago and currently used by farmers, some crops can coexist with the forest, if you find the right balance. Although not technically reforestation, agroforestry (a system of land use in which harvestable trees or shrubs are grown among or around crops or on pasture land, as a means of preserving or enhancing the productivity of the land) provides an opportunity for small-holder farmers to sustain their livelihoods while adding some forest cover to their farms.
zh: 本段把讨论从大型项目延伸到 smallholder farms，说明森林恢复也可以融入日常农业生产，并兼顾 community benefits。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: A global project called Breedcafs is studying how trees behave in coffee farms, hoping to find crop varieties that manage to grow under the shade of trees. Coffee grows naturally in such forests, so copying that in farms is taking the crop back to its roots. "By reintroducing trees in the landscape, we impact positively humidity, rain capture, soil conservation and biodiversity preservation," says coffee expert Benoit Bertrand, who leads the project from the French Agricultural Research Centre for International Development. Bertrand is analysing which of dozens of coffee varieties fits better for this system. A similar approach can be applied to land with cocoa, vanilla and fruit trees.
zh: 本段用咖啡这一具体 example 进一步证明 agroforestry 的可行性，把农业生产、生态功能和作物选择联系起来。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Not every piece of land is fit for reforestation. Vergara's partners look for safe investments, and even Land Life Company only runs major projects in what they consider "low-risk" countries. "We tend to avoid large-scale operations in countries in some parts of the Middle East or Africa where the permanence is not secured," says Ruys.
zh: 本段为前文较为积极的案例加入 necessary limitation，强调生态修复必须考虑政治稳定、投资风险和长期成果保障。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: But in the right location, perhaps all you need is time. In the Central Pacific of Costa Rica, the 330-hectare National Wildlife Refuge Baru looks nothing like the cattle ranch it was before 1987, when Jack Ewing decided to turn this large estate into an ecotourism destination. Instead of intervening, a friend told him to let nature have its way. Baru's former grazing lands are now thriving woods and the property boasts over 150 hectares of secondary forests with no intervention from humans. In the past 10 years, animals such as howling monkeys, scarlet macaws and even migratory cougars have returned to the refuge's land, boosting tourism and revitalising the ecosystem. Ewing, now 75, explains this success using the words his friend chose three decades ago: "In Costa Rica, when you stop managing the shrubs, the jungle comes back for its revenge."
zh: 本段以 Costa Rica 的成功案例收尾，与前文的 technology-based restoration 形成互补，最终强调生态修复可以依靠技术、投资，也可以依靠时间和自然力量。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Smartphones have always posed challenges for parents of teens. From social media apps to excessive screen time, the digital world is as threatening as the physical.
zh: 本段承担 introduction 的功能，先建立 smartphones 与 teen safety 之间的争议背景，为下文讨论 explicit content、mental health 和 parental action 提供总入口。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: A new study shows that about half of parents of teens are worried about their teens being exposed to explicit content online. This is a valid concern, of course. But there are ways to alleviate the spread of explicit content, from changing the settings in their kids' phone to monitoring such content with apps like Bark.
zh: 本段把首段的笼统网络危险具体化为 explicit content，并首次提出 parental monitoring 的应对方向，直接支撑全文关于父母应积极管理手机使用的中心主旨。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Just as alarming, if not more so, is that the amount of time teens spend on social media can lead to anxiety and depression.
zh: 本段是全文论证的转轴，它将话题从可监控的内容安全问题推进到更深层的 mental health problem，并为后两段说明屏幕时间危害奠定论点。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Excessive screen time has detrimental effects, for a lot of obvious reasons. Constant media consumption inhibits healthy activities associated with childhood, like spending time outside, exercising, talking to friends and family. If it interferes with sleep, that's even worse.
zh: 本段通过日常生活层面的 consequences 解释为何 excessive screen time 有害，使上一段的心理健康论断不再抽象，并突出线下健康活动的必要性。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Ample research shows too much smartphone use produces significant anxiety, depression, and feelings of isolation in teens. Teens log on to social media or spend time online trying to make connections, but end up feeling more alone and sad than ever. Faceless communication not only produces feelings of isolation and loneliness but increases instances of online bullying and susceptibility to criminal conducts.
zh: 本段是全文最核心的证据段，它用 research 和具体机制充分证明 smartphones 不只是带来轻微不便，而会造成 anxiety、depression、isolation 及网络欺凌等复合伤害。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Though I've banned most social media, I've still battled smartphone time with my own kids. A lot of the time I wish I could throw my kids' smartphones into the nearest lake. The convenience of communication—when they need a ride home from school after practice, for instance—often feels like it isn't worth the battle to keep their screen time low and productive, and continue to encourage "real-life" activities outside and with friends and family. I understand the addiction and often tell them I'm not sure how I would have handled having a smartphone as a teen. As an adult, I too, struggle with overuse.
zh: 本段用作者自身家庭的案例补足前文的理论论证，说明即使认识到危害并主动限制 social media，父母仍会受到手机便利性和成瘾性的现实制约。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: In a recent TV interview to promote a new film about a mother and daughter navigating social media use, actress Kate Winslet expressed her view on teens and social media—and her concern mirrors the trends. "I do definitely feel that the world of social media is frightening to parents because we don't really know what's there," she said. "We don't know how our children are using it. We don't know the effects that it's really having on them."
zh: 本段通过 public figure 的观点印证父母普遍存在的担忧，将作者的个人经历扩展为更广泛的社会 concern，并增强全文论证的共鸣与可信度。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: I don't think the U.S. government should regulate social media and teen smartphone use, but it is a vital topic for parents to understand and take seriously. Unfortunately, now, parents don't just have to worry about real-world dangers, but all the ones sneaking online and the effects they have on teenagers and their mental health.
zh: 本段完成全文 conclusion：它回收 explicit online dangers、smartphone use 和 mental health 等前文论点，并把最终责任落在 parents 身上，与文章主旨中的 monitor usage 和 encourage balanced offline lives 完全一致。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: What does self-discipline look like at work? Sometimes, it's the ability to resist temptation, such as distractions to avoid a particular task. Other times it's the ability to persist with a task when your energy and motivation seem low.
zh: 本段为全文搭建 self-discipline 的讨论对象，使后文关于 willpower 是否会耗尽的 research、mindset 和 strategies 都有明确的指向。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: What do you believe about the nature of your own self-discipline? Is it something that runs on internal energy that is spent with use? Or is it something that is bolstered as you apply it and persist?
zh: 本段把第一段的自律现象转化为一个 mindset question，为第三段说明“不同信念为何导致不同体验”预先设定论证框架。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: Your answer matters, as it determines how much self-discipline you experience. For years, research in psychology pointed to self-control as a resource that is depleted with use and needs to be restored through breaks, rest, or sleep. More recently, however, research points to the importance of mindset. If you view self-discipline as an expendable resource, your willpower tends to fade with use. If you believe that exercising your self-control strengthens and fuels it, that is more likely to be your experience as you resist temptation or push yourself to get something done that is not appealing.
zh: 本段是全文的 central argument，它把第二段提出的两种看法与不同的行为结果建立因果联系，并为后文的改变信念和训练方法提供理论依据。
note_type: 原句所在段的理解提示

en: If you don't already view self-discipline as a force that feeds itself, what might you do? Reflect on times that you had initial difficulty resisting temptation, getting started on something, or sticking with it, but pushed ahead and accomplished the task or met the goal.
